ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p47/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p47/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p47/r1.claim: The claim that «We record their traces» was revealed about Banū Salima considering a move near the Prophet’s mosque is unsound; another exception proposed is the spending verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p47/r1.anchor: حين أرادوا أن يتركوا ديارهم وينتقلوا إلى جوار مسجد الرسول، وليس زعما صحيحا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r6.claim: After messengerhood, the passage names resurrection, another of the three foundations of faith; the third is divine unity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r6.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى الرسالة، وهي أحد الأصول الثلاثة التي بها يصير المكلف مؤمنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r7.claim: «We give life to the dead» means raising them after death; al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk’s interpretation as bringing people from shirk to faith is far-fetched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r7.anchor: وأبعد الحسن والضحاك في قوله: إحياؤهم: إخراجهم من الشرك إلى الإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r8.claim: Recording what people did is a metaphor for recompense and for the comprehensive knowledge fixed by writing; another recitation uses a passive verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r8.anchor: ونكتب ما قدموا، كناية عن المجازاة: أي ونحصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r9.speaker: زر ومسروق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r9.claim: They read «and it is written» in the passive; «their traces» are their footsteps to the mosques.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p51/r9.anchor: وقرأ زر ومسروق: ويكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم بالياء مبنيا للمفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r1.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r1.claim: He explains the recorded traces as good and bad paths; another view distinguishes their prior bad deeds from the deeds left as traces.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r1.anchor: وقال: السير الحسنة والسيئة. وقيل: ما قدموا من السيئات وآثارهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r2.claim: He includes lasting effects left after death: useful knowledge, books, endowments, buildings, or harmful policies, debased coinage, distractions, and any good or bad custom others follow.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r2.anchor: وما هلكوا عنه من أثر حسن، كعلم علموه، وكتاب صنفوه، أو حبيس أحبسوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r3.claim: Most read «every thing» in the accusative by the resumptive construction; Abū al-Sammāl reads it nominative as a new subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وكل شيء بالنصب على الاشتغال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r4.speaker: مجاهد، وقتادة، وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r4.claim: They identify the «clear register» as the Preserved Tablet; another group understands it as records of deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p52/r4.anchor: والإمام المبين: اللوح المحفوظ، قاله مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p376/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p376/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p376/r3.claim: God will resurrect the dead and record their deeds and traces; this entails judgment according to deeds, an implication left unstated because it is evident, while deniers doubt resurrection and another aspect of judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p376/r3.anchor: this necessarily means that He will deal with each of them according to his or her deeds

ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r20.claim: God's “We” expresses majesty and might, or means “We alone.”
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r20.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın “Biz” buyurması azamet içindir, yani azamet şânımız olan Biz izzet ve kudreti mâlum olan Allahız, yahut Biz başka değil yalnız Biz

ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r21.claim: God records all good and bad deeds people perform in life and all beneficial or harmful traces they leave, including institutions, learning, books, and corrupting laws or examples.
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r21.anchor: ve takdim ettikleri şeyleri hayatlarında yaptıkları iyi ve kötü bütün amelleri

ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r22.speaker: Peygamber
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r22.claim: A sound hadith says a person's deeds cease at death except for ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, and a righteous child who prays for them.
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r22.anchor: öldüğü vakit ameli munkatı‘olur, şu üçten başka: Sadaka-i câriye, intifâ‘olunur ilim, ona dua eden sâlih evlad.

ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r23.claim: The hadith identifies kinds of lasting good works, while the verse also says that their harmful counterparts are recorded.
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r23.anchor: bu hadîs-i şerîf kalacak hayırlı eserlerin aksâmını beyan etmiştir. Âyet bunların zıddı olan kötü eserlerin de yazılacağını beyan ediyor

ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r24.claim: The Clear Register is the Preserved Tablet, the main book in which everything is counted.
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r24.anchor: önce açık bir kütükte, bir ana kitabda, yani Levh-i Mahfûz’da ihsâ etmişizdir.

ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r25.claim: All things are known to God and recorded in the Preserved Tablet before occurring, then written after occurrence with their traces so people are held responsible.
ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r25.anchor: her şey, vukū‘undan evvel ilm-i ilâhîde mâlum olup Levh-i Mahfûz’da bütün sayısıyla zabtedilmiş olmakla beraber vukū‘undan sonra da bütün izleri ve gölgeleriyle

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r5.claim: God raises the dead at resurrection and records the good and evil deeds people sent ahead.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r5.anchor: {إنا نحن نحيي الموتى} ، عند البعث، {ونكتب ما قدموا} من الأعمال من خير وشر،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r6.claim: Their traces are the good or bad practices they established.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r6.anchor: {وآثارهم} أي: ما سنوا من سنة حسنة أو سيئة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r7.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r7.claim: The Prophet says whoever establishes a good practice followed by others receives a matching reward without reducing theirs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r7.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من سن في الإسلام سنة حسنة يعمل بها من بعده كان له أجرها ومثل أجر من عمل بها من بعده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r8.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r8.claim: The Prophet says whoever establishes a bad practice bears its sin and the matching sins of those who follow it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r8.anchor: ومن سن في الإسلام سنة سيئة كان عليه وزرها ووزر من عمل بها من بعده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r9.speaker: قوم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r9.claim: Some say the traces are the footsteps people take to the mosque.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r9.anchor: وقال قوم: قوله: "ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم" أي: خطاهم إلى المسجد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r10.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that after Banu Salama complained about the mosque's distance, this verse was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r10.anchor: روي عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: شكت بنو سلمة بعد منازلهم من المسجد فأنزل الله تعالى: "ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r11.speaker: أنس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r11.claim: Anas reports that Banu Salama stayed after the Prophet urged them to count their footsteps rather than move nearer the mosque.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p9#2/r11.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: "أرادت بنو سلمة أن يتحولوا إلى قرب المسجد، فكره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن تعرى المدينة، فقال: يا بني سلمة ألا تحتسبون آثاركم؟ فأقاموا"

DURR-FULL:v7p45/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p45/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v7p45/r8.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that the verse was revealed when the Banu Salama wanted to move near the mosque; the Prophet said their footsteps were recorded, so they stayed. Al-Tirmidhi graded the report hasan and al-Hakim authenticated it.
DURR-FULL:v7p45/r8.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: كان بنو سلمة في ناحية من المدينة فأرادوا أن ينتقلوا إلى قرب المسجد فأنزل الله

DURR-FULL:v7p45/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p45/r9.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v7p45/r9.claim: Abu Saʿid glosses the “traces” recorded in the verse as footsteps.
DURR-FULL:v7p45/r9.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه {إنا نحن نحيي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم} قال: الخطا

DURR-FULL:v7p45/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p45/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p45/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says the distant homes of the Ansar led them to consider moving nearer the mosque, but after this verse was revealed they chose to stay.
DURR-FULL:v7p45/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كانت الأنصار منازلهم بعيدة من المسجد فأرادوا أن ينتقلوا قريبا من المسجد فنزلت

DURR-FULL:v7p45/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p45/r11.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v7p45/r11.claim: Jabir says the Banu Salama wished to sell their homes and move near the mosque, but the Prophet told them to stay because their footsteps were recorded.
DURR-FULL:v7p45/r11.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: إن بني سلمة أرادوا أن يبيعوا ديارهم ويتحولوا قريبا من المسجد فقال لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r10.claim: God’s raising of the dead answers the disbelievers’ denial; recording their deeds and traces warns them that all they do is counted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r10.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى بإحيائه الموتى ردا على الكفرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r11.claim: Deeds and traces overlap, but both are named to emphasize what endures and is remembered as well as what a person did, good or evil.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r11.anchor: فيدخل فيما قدم ويدخل في آثاره لكنه تعالى ذكر الأمر من الجهتين ولينبه على الآثار التي تبقى ويذكر ما قدم الإنسان من خير أو شر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r12.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r12.claim: Qatāda, Ibn Zayd, and Mujāhid explain ‘what they sent ahead’ as their deeds; a person may leave a practice that others follow after death, earning reward or sin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r12.anchor: وقال قتادة ما قدموا معناه من عمل، وقاله ابن زيد ومجاهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r13.claim: He links the wording to the verse ‘a soul will know what it sent ahead and left behind’ in 82:5 and to the statement ‘man will be informed…’ in 75:13.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p447#3/r13.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية علمت نفس ما قدمت وأخرت

JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r3.claim: Iḥṣāʾ means counting, from the verb aḥṣā yuḥṣī, to count.
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r3.anchor: الإحصاء: العد، أحصى يحصي، أي: عد

JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r4.claim: An imām is one followed; its root carries the sense of intending, and a book is called an imām because it is followed.
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r4.anchor: والإمام: من يؤتم به، وأصله: القصد، أم يؤم أما، وسمي الكتاب إماما؛ لأنه يؤتم به

JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r6.claim: The revelation concerning āthāra was about Banū ʿUdhra, whose homes were far from the mosque and who found attendance at prayer difficult; their footprints are meant.
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r6.anchor: نزل قوله: (وآثارهم) في بني عذرة، كانت منازلهم بعيدة من المسجد، فشق عليهم حضور الصلوات

JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r7.claim: Another view takes the wording about their traces as general rather than specific to Banū ʿUdhra.

JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r12.claim: God gives life to the dead for recompense on the Day of Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r12.anchor: إنا نحن نحي الموتى للجزاء يوم القيامة

JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r13.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r13.claim: Mujāhid explains the phrase about giving life to the dead as referring to deeds.
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r13.anchor: إنا نحن نحي الموتى أي: الأعمال، عن مجاهد

JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r14.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r14.claim: Abū ʿAlī distinguishes deeds without continuing effects, which are what people sent ahead, from deeds that leave continuing effects, which are their traces.
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r14.anchor: ما قدموا من أعمال ليس لها أثر وآثارهم ما له أثر، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r15.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r15.claim: One interpretation of traces is the practices people leave behind, whether good or bad.
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r15.anchor: آثارهم قيل: أعمالهم التي صارت سنة بعدهم

JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r16.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r16.claim: Abū Muslim interprets the traces as wealth people leave behind.
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r16.anchor: وقيل: ما خلفوه من الأموال، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r17.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r17.claim: The phrase about recording everything can mean that God knows it or that He has counted it.
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r17.anchor: وكل شيء أحصيناه قيل: علمناه، وقيل: عددناه

JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r18.claim: The clear register is the Preserved Tablet, God's book for the angels; it is called an imām because it is followed or because it is first and precedes the others.
JISHUMI:v8p5870#2/r18.anchor: في إمام مبين أي: كتاب مبين، وهو اللوح المحفوظ، كتاب الله للملائكة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r14.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r14.claim: God brings the dead to life by giving faith after disbelief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r14.anchor: نحييهم بالإيمان بعد الكفر , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r15.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r15.claim: God brings the dead to life through resurrection for recompense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r15.anchor: الثاني : بالبعث للجزاء , قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r16.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r16.claim: What people send ahead is their good or evil deeds; their traces are precedents they leave that others follow.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r16.anchor: ما قدموا هو ما عملوا من خير أو شر , وآثارهم ما أثروا من سنة حسنة أو سيئة يعمل بها بعدهم , قاله سعيد بن جبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r17.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r17.claim: He interprets what they send ahead as their deeds and their traces as their footsteps to mosques.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r17.anchor: ما قدموا : أعمالهم , وآثارهم : خطاهم إلى المساجد , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r18.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r18.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that Banu Salima considered moving nearer the mosque; after this verse came, the Prophet said their footsteps were recorded, so they stayed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r18.anchor: روى سفيان عن أبي نضرة عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال : كانت بنو سلمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r19.claim: If the reported occasion is not established, traces may mean people are repaired or corrupted after them through their righteousness or corruption.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r19.anchor: ويحتمل إن لم يثبت نقل هذا السبب تأويلا ثالثا أن آثارهم هو أن يصلح من صاحبهم بصلاحهم , أو يفسد بفسادهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r20.claim: The phrase 'We have enumerated everything' can mean that God knows everything.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r20.anchor: { وكل شيء أحصيناه } فيه وجهان : أحدهما : علمناه

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r21.claim: Alternatively, it can mean that God preserves everything.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r22.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r22.claim: He identifies the clear register with the Preserved Tablet.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r23.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r23.claim: He identifies the clear register with the Mother of the Book.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r24.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r24.claim: He interprets the clear register as a straight path.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p8/r24.anchor: الثالث : معناه طريق مستقيم , قاله الضحاك

NAHHAS:v3p385/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p385/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p385/r14.claim: In إننا, one nūn is omitted because the nūns would otherwise come together.

NAHHAS:v3p385/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p385/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p385/r15.claim: In نحيي, the ḍamma is omitted because it is heavy, and the two yāʾs cannot be assimilated because that would bring two vowelless letters together.
NAHHAS:v3p385/r15.anchor: حذفت منه الضمة لثقلها ولا يجوز إدغام الياء في الياء

NAHHAS:v3p385/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p385/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p385/r16.claim: ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم means recording what people sent ahead; the genitive complement stands in place of an omitted governing noun.
NAHHAS:v3p385/r16.anchor: أي ذكر ما قدموا وأقيم المضاف إليه مقام المضاف

NAHHAS:v3p385/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p385/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v3p385/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets آثارهم as their footsteps to the mosques.
NAHHAS:v3p385/r17.anchor: وتأوله ابن عباس بمعنى خطاهم إلى المساجد

NAHHAS:v3p385/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p385/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p385/r18.claim: Abu Jaafar calls the footsteps interpretation the strongest because the verse was revealed about the Ansar, whose homes were far from the mosque.
NAHHAS:v3p385/r18.anchor: وهو أولى ما قيل فيه لأنه قال إن الآية نزلت في ذلك لأن الأنصار كانت منازلهم بعيدة من المسجد

NAHHAS:v3p385/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p385/r19.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NAHHAS:v3p385/r19.claim: A report from Uqba ibn Amir says each step on the way to or from the mosque earns a good deed and erases a bad deed.
NAHHAS:v3p385/r19.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يكتب له برجل حسنة ويحط عنه برجل سيئة ذاهبا وراجعا

NAHHAS:v3p385/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p385/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p385/r20.claim: Other interpreters take آثارهم as good deeds people sent ahead and good practices they initiated that others continued.
NAHHAS:v3p385/r20.anchor: وتأوله غير ابن عباس ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم يعني نكتب ما قدموا من خير وما سنوا من سنة حسنة يعمل بها بعدهم

NAHHAS:v3p385/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p385/r21.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p385/r21.claim: The singular of آثار is أثر, also pronounced إثر.

NAHHAS:v3p385/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p385/r22.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p385/r22.claim: كل شيء أحصيناه may be nominative as a subject, but Abu Jaafar prefers the accusative because it coordinates an object of the verb with other objects; this is also Khalil and Sibawayh's analysis.
NAHHAS:v3p385/r22.anchor: منصوب على إضمار فعل ويجوز رفعه بالابتداء إلا أن نصبه أولى ليعطف ما عمل فيه الفعل على ما عمل فيه الفعل وهذا قول الخليل وسيبويه

NAHHAS:v3p385/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p385/r23.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v3p385/r23.claim: Mujahid identifies the clear register as the Preserved Tablet.
NAHHAS:v3p385/r23.anchor: قال مجاهد ( في إمام مبين ) في اللوح المحفوظ

MUQATIL:36:11-12/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:11-12/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:11-12/r3.claim: God raises the dead in the next life and records the good and evil people did during their lives.
MUQATIL:36:11-12/r3.anchor: فى الآخرة { ونكتب ما قدموا } فى الدنيا فى حياتهم من خير أو شر عملوه

MUQATIL:36:11-12/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:11-12/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:11-12/r4.claim: Their traces are good or evil practices they established and others followed after their death; each founder receives a like reward or burden without any reduction to others’ shares.
MUQATIL:36:11-12/r4.anchor: ما استنوه من سنة خير أو شر فاقتدى به من بعد موتهم، وإن كان خيرا فله مثل أجر من عمل به،

MUQATIL:36:11-12/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:11-12/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:11-12/r5.claim: The statement that a person will be told what he sent ahead and left behind is a parallel to this account of deeds and their traces.
MUQATIL:36:11-12/r5.anchor:
فذلك قوله عز وجل:
ينبأ الإنسان يومئذ بما قدم وأخر
[القيامة: 13]

MUQATIL:36:11-12/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:11-12/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:11-12/r6.claim: Everything people do is counted in the Preserved Tablet, the clear register.
MUQATIL:36:11-12/r6.anchor: كل شىء عملوه فى اللوح المحفوظ.

TABATABAI:36:1-12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r1.claim: The verse about the book speaking truthfully and recording deeds supports the claim that people's actions are preserved.
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r1.anchor: هذا كتابنا ينطق عليكم بالحق إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون الجاثية 29.

TABATABAI:36:1-12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r2.claim: He rejects identifying the Clear Register with records of deeds.
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r2.anchor: وقيل المراد بالإمام المبين صحف الأعمال وليس بشيء

TABATABAI:36:1-12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r3.claim: He likewise rejects interpreting it as God's knowledge, except that the interpretation has merit if it means God's active, causal knowledge.
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r3.anchor: وقيل علمه تعالى وهو كسابقه نعم لو أريد به العلم الفعلي كان له وجه.

TABATABAI:36:1-12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r4.claim: Some say the Preserved Tablet records events only through the Resurrection, since a finite physical body cannot contain an infinite series of events.
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r4.anchor: ومن عجيب القول في هذا المقام ما ذكره بعضهم أن الذي كتب في اللوح المحفوظ هو ما كان وما يكون إلى يوم القيامة لا حوادث العالم إلى أبد الآبدين

TABATABAI:36:1-12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r5.claim: Their argument is that the Tablet is a body with finite dimensions, so recording everything about infinite events in it at once is impossible; they accordingly limit everything to events through the Resurrection.
TABATABAI:36:1-12/r5.anchor: وبيان كل شيء فيه على الوجه المعروف عندنا دفعة مقتض لكون المتناهي ظرفا لغير المتناهي وهو محال بالبديهة

TABATABAI:36:1-12#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:1-12#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:1-12#2/r1.claim: He calls arbitrary the proposal to restrict everything recorded to events through the Resurrection.

ZAJJAJ:v4p281/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p281/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p281/r4.claim: The recorded traces include the consequences of good or bad precedents: whoever establishes a good practice receives its reward, and whoever establishes an evil one bears its penalty.
ZAJJAJ:v4p281/r4.anchor:
من سن سنة حسنة
كتب له ثوابها، ومن سن سنة سيئة كتب عليه عقابها

ZAJJAJ:v4p281/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p281/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p281/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes the recorded traces to mean people's footsteps; Zajjāj prefers the precedent-and-consequences explanation as more common and clearer.
ZAJJAJ:v4p281/r5.anchor: وقد قيل: (وتكتب آثارهم) أي خطاهم، والأول أكثر وأبين

THALABI:v8p122/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p122/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p122/r5.claim: God will resurrect the dead and record their deeds and traces, including what they leave behind; the author links this to verses about what people send ahead and leave behind.
THALABI:v8p122/r5.anchor: إنا نحن نحي الموتى عند البعث ونكتب ما قدموا من الأعمال وآثارهم ما استن به بعدهم

THALABI:v8p122/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p122/r6.speaker: المغيرة بن شعبة
THALABI:v8p122/r6.claim: Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba says the verse was revealed about Banu Udhra, whose distance from the mosque made attending prayers difficult; their recorded traces are their steps to the mosque.
THALABI:v8p122/r6.anchor: وقال المغيرة بن شعبة والضحاك: نزلت في بني عذرة، وكانت منازلهم بعيدة عن المسجد

THALABI:v8p122/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p122/r7.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v8p122/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak likewise identifies Banu Udhra as the occasion: their homes were far from the mosque, and the recorded traces are their footsteps there.
THALABI:v8p122/r7.anchor: وقال المغيرة بن شعبة والضحاك: نزلت في بني عذرة، وكانت منازلهم بعيدة عن المسجد

THALABI:v8p122#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p122#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v8p122#2/r1.claim: Abdullah recounts that Banu Salama wanted to move nearer the mosque; the Prophet told them to remain, since their footsteps would be recorded, and they accepted.
THALABI:v8p122#2/r1.anchor: عن جابر عن عبد الله قال: أردنا النقلة إلى المسجد والبقاع حول المسجد خالية

THALABI:v8p122#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p122#2/r2.speaker: أنس
THALABI:v8p122#2/r2.claim: Anas explains the recorded traces as the steps taken to Friday prayer.
THALABI:v8p122#2/r2.anchor: عن ثابت عن أنس في قوله سبحانه: ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم قال: الخطى يوم الجمعة

THALABI:v8p122#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p122#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p122#2/r3.claim: The “clear register” is the Preserved Tablet, in which God knows, counts, and makes clear everything.
THALABI:v8p122#2/r3.anchor: وكل شيء أحصيناه علمناه وعددناه وبيناه في إمام مبين وهو اللوح المحفوظ

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r2.claim: At resurrection God records people's deeds and their traces, meaning what they leave others to follow.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r2.anchor: ونكتب ما قدموا } من الأعمال { وآثارهم } ما استن به بعدهم.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r3.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes the recorded traces to mean the steps people take to mosques.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r3.anchor: آثارهم } ما استن به بعدهم. وقيل: خطاهم إلى المساجد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r4.claim: God has counted and clarified everything in the manifest register, the Preserved Tablet.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r4.anchor: وكل شيء أحصيناه } عددناه وبيناه { في إمام مبين } وهو اللوح المحفوظ.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802/r9.claim: God's reviving the dead refers to resurrection.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802/r9.anchor: إنا نحن نحيي الموتى} [يس: 12] ، يعني: البعث.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802/r10.claim: The record of what people sent ahead and left behind is linked to 82:5.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802/r10.anchor: {ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم} [يس: 12] كقوله: {علمت نفس ما قدمت وأخرت} [الانفطار: 5] .

SAMIN-DURR:36:12/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:12/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:36:12/r1.claim: The common active reading makes ما قدموا the object of نكتب and coordinates آثارهم with it.
SAMIN-DURR:36:12/r1.anchor: قوله: { ونكتب }: العامة على بنائه للفاعل، فيكون " ما قدموا " مفعولا به، و " آثارهم " عطف عليه.

SAMIN-DURR:36:12/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:12/r2.speaker: زر ومسروق
SAMIN-DURR:36:12/r2.claim: Zirr and Masruq read passively, with آثارهم nominative and coordinated with ما قدموا as deputy subject.
SAMIN-DURR:36:12/r2.anchor: وزر ومسروق مبنيا للمفعول، و " آثارهم " بالرفع، عطف على " ما قدموا " لقيامه مقام الفاعل.

SAMIN-DURR:36:12/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:12/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:12/r3.claim: The common accusative parses وكل شيء as الاشتغال; Abu al-Simal reads a nominative subject, but the author prefers the accusative to coordinate two verbal clauses.
SAMIN-DURR:36:12/r3.anchor: قوله: { وكل شيء أحصيناه } العامة على نصبه على الاشتغال. وأبو السمال قرأه مرفوعا بالابتداء. والأرجح قراءة العامة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p292/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p292/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p292/r1.claim: At Mecca, Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq challenged Ibn ʿAbbās's answers; Ibn ʿAbbās replied that worse are those who speak without knowledge or conceal knowledge, then invited questions.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p292/r1.anchor: فقال له ابن عباس: ثكلتك أمك يا نافع، وعَدمَتْك، ألا أخبرك من هو أجرأ مني؟

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p292/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p292/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p292/r2.claim: The recension through Juwaybir from al-Ḍaḥḥāk contains thirty-one questions; the same location and count appear in al-Ṭabarānī's additions.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p292/r2.anchor: وساق المسائل والجواب عنها والشواهد عليها، وعددها عنده

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p292/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p292/r3.speaker: البدر الزركشي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p292/r3.claim: Al-Zarkashī calls knowledge of rare Qur'anic vocabulary necessary for an exegete and says one may not interpret without it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p292/r3.anchor: معرفة هذا الفن للمفسر ضروري، وإلا فلا يحل له الإقدام على كتاب الله تعالى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p299/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p299/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p299/r1.claim: An old Damascus recension by al-Khuṭallī preserves the Ibn al-Azraq encounter and fifty questions; another recension through Abū Shihāb and ʿIkrima tells substantially the same story.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p299/r1.anchor: أما نسخة الظاهرية بدمشق فأصل عتيق، من رواية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p299/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p299/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p299/r2.claim: The Damascus manuscript is attributed to Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Salm al-Khuṭallī, an intermediary from the third and fourth centuries.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p299/r2.anchor: أما نسخة الظاهرية بدمشق فأصل عتيق، من رواية "أبي بكر أحمد بن جعفر ابن محمد بن سَلْم الخُتَّلى"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p299/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p299/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p299/r3.claim: The segment then introduces a third recension of the questions, transmitted through ʿUthmān.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p299/r3.anchor: ثم في صفحة (115 و) بعنوان مسائل ابن الأزرق، رواية ثالثة لها من طريق عثمان

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p300/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p300/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p300/r1.claim: A third recension through ʿUthmān al-Ḥarrānī gives fifty questions and redirects the question about makāʾ and taṣdiyah to al-Kalbī.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p300/r1.anchor: فذكر الخبر والمسائل، وعددها خمسون مسألة كذلك

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p300/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p300/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p300/r2.claim: The manuscript is difficult to read but carries extensive audition and correction records from leading scholars.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p300/r2.anchor: على هذه الصفحة ألأولى، تصحيح سماع لطبقات من الأعلام والحفاظ الأئمة، منها سماع الشيخ أبي الحسين المبارك

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#4/r1.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#4/r1.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote that if anything were left unrecorded for a person, it would be the traces erased by the winds, underscoring that even such traces are recorded.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#4/r1.anchor: كتب عمر بن عبد العزيز لو كان الله تاركا لابن آدم شيئا لترك له ما عفت عليه الرياح من أثرة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#4/r2.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#4/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the traces include every deed that has gone before, good or evil.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#4/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي ﴿ آثارهم ﴾ كل شيء سبق من خير أو شر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#4/r3.speaker: مسروق بن الأجدع
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#4/r3.claim: Masruq ibn al-Ajdaʿ says every step a person takes is recorded as a good deed or a sin.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#4/r3.anchor: عن الأعمش عن أبي الضحى عن مسروق بن الأجدع قال ما خطا رجل خطوة إلا كتبت حسنة أو سيئة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r1.claim: The verse closes the preceding discussion for resolute disbelievers and those helped by warning, combining threat and promise, deterrence and encouragement.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r1.anchor: تذييل عام للفريقين المصممين على الكفر والمشفعين بالإنذار ترهيبا وترغيبا ووعيدا ووعدا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r2.claim: Repeating نحن conveys exclusivity or emphasis; al-Alusi notes a subtle mirrored quality in its use.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r2.anchor: وتكرير الضمير لإفادة الحصر أو للتقوية وما ألطف هذا الضمير الذي عكسه كطرده ههنا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r3.claim: The majestic plural signals the act's greatness; emphasis attends to the report or answers deniers who claimed no resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r3.anchor: وضمير العظمة للإشارة إلى جلالة الفعل والتأكيد للاعتناء بأمر الخبر أو لرد الإنكار

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r4.claim: God will resurrect all the dead on Judgment Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r4.anchor: أي إنا نحن نحيي الأموات جميعا ببعثهم يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r5.claim: What people sent ahead means their good and bad deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r5.anchor: ( ما أسلفوه من الأعمال الصالحة والطالحة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r6.claim: Continuing traces include taught knowledge, books, endowed property, and charitable buildings left behind.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r6.anchor: من الحسنات كعلم علموه أو كتاب القوه أو حبيس وقفوه أو بناء في سبيل الله تعالى بنوه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r7.claim: Traces also include harmful legacies: injustice and foundations of evil and corruption set up for others.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r7.anchor: ومن السيئات كتأسيس قوانين الظلم والعدوان وترتيب مباديء الشر والفساد فيما بين العباد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r8.speaker: جرير بن عبدالله البجلي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r8.claim: Jarir reports the Prophet said whoever begins good earns its and followers' rewards without diminution, while an evil initiator bears its and followers' sins; the Prophet recited this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r8.anchor: أخرج إبن أبي حاتم عن جرير بن عبدالله البجلي قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من سن سنة حسنة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r9.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r9.claim: Anas interprets the traces as footsteps on Friday.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r9.anchor: وعن أنس أنه قال في الآية : هذا في الخطو يوم الجمعة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r10.claim: Some commentators extend the footsteps interpretation to walking to mosques generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r10.anchor: وفسر بعضهم الآثار بالخطا إلى المساجد مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r11.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r11.claim: Abu Saʿid reports Banu Salima wanted to move nearer the mosque; the Prophet said their steps were recorded, recited the verse, and they stayed. Al-Tirmidhi graded the report hasan.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r11.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال كان بنو سلمة في ناحية من المدينة فأرادوا أن ينتقلوا إلى قرب المسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Ansar wanted to move nearer the mosque; after the verse came down they chose to remain.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#2/r12.anchor: عن إبن عباس قال كانت الأنصار منازلهم بعيدة من المسجد فأرادوا أن ينتقلوا قريبا من المسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r1.claim: Footsteps are one kind of trace, not the exclusive meaning; al-Alusi reads the word broadly.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r1.anchor: لا دلالة فيما ذكر على أن الآثار هي الخطا لا غير وقصارى ما يدل عليه أنها من الآثار فلتحمل الآثار على ما يعمها وغيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r2.claim: The reports and similar accounts are used to argue that the verse was revealed in Medina.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r2.anchor: وأستدل بهذين الخبرين ونحوهما على أن الآية مدنية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the claim that the reports establish a Medinan revelation and cites contrary evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r3.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : ليس ذلك زعما صحيحا وشنع عليه بما ورد مما يدل على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r4.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r4.claim: Al-Khafaji defends Abu Hayyan, saying the report is countered by the Sahihayn account where the Prophet recited the verse without saying it was newly revealed to those people.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r4.anchor: وانتصر له الخفاجي بأن الحديث الدال معارض بما في الصحيحين أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ لهم هذه الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r5.claim: Al-Alusi says the earlier reports plainly describe revelation then, whereas the Sahihayn recitation does not prove later revelation; he faults al-Khafaji for missing this distinction.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r5.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الحديثين السابقين ظاهران في ان الآية نزلت يومئذ وليس في حديث الصحيحين ما يعارض ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r6.claim: Another interpretation takes what they sent ahead as intentions and their traces as deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r6.anchor: وقيل ما قدموا من النيات وآثارهم من الأعمال

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r7.claim: Writing most naturally means entry in angel records, attributed to God because it is by His command and mentioned after resurrection because its effect appears then; interpreting the deeds as intentions is weakened by reports that angels cannot see or record them.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالكتابة الكتابة في صحف الملائكة الكرام الكاتبين ولكونها بأمره عزوجل أسندت إليه سبحانه وأخرت في الذكر عن الأحياء

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r8.claim: Some explain writing as preserving deeds in God's knowledge without forgetting or neglecting them.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r8.anchor: وفسر بعضهم الكتابة بالحفظ أي نحفظ ذلك ونثبته في علمنا لا ننساه ولا نهمله

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r9.claim: Al-Alusi prefers taking writing as a metonym for recompense, good for good and evil for evil; this explains why it follows resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r9.anchor: ولعلك تختار أن كتابة ما قدموا وآثارهم كناية عن مجازاتهم عليها إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r10.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r10.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak take reviving the dead as bringing people from shirk to faith, death metaphorically meaning ignorance; al-Alusi calls this remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r10.anchor: وعن الحسن والضحاك أن أحياء الله تعالى الموتى أن يخرجهم من الشرك إلى الإيمان وجعلا الموت مجازا عن الجهل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r11.speaker: زر ومسروق
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r11.claim: Zirr and Masruq read ويكتب in the passive with yāʾ and آثارهم in the nominative.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r11.anchor: وقرأ زر ومسروق ( ويكتب ) بالياء مبنيا للمفعول ( وآثارهم ) بالفرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r12.claim: كل شيء covers all things; ihsāʾ originally means counting and extends to clarifying and preserving.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r12.anchor: من الأشياء كائنا ما كان والنصب على الاشتغال أي وأحصينا كل شيء ( أحصيناه ( أي بيناه وحفظناه وأصل الإحصاء العد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r13.claim: He parses وكل شيء accusatively by اشتغال, with an understood وأحصينا كل شيء.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p218#3/r13.anchor: والنصب على الاشتغال أي وأحصينا كل شيء ( أحصيناه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r1.claim: An imam is a great source or register that is followed and obeyed; mubīn makes past and future matters manifest.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r1.anchor: ( أي أصل عظيم الشأن يؤتم ويقتدي به ويتبع ولا يخالف ( مبين

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r2.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r2.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd identify the clear register as the Preserved Tablet.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r2.anchor: وهو على ما في البحر حكاية عن مجاهد وقتادة وإبن زيد اللوح المحفوظ

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r3.claim: If the universal includes Paradise's unending events, the Tablet could record them in successive installments, like the higher account in the Jafr al-Jamiʿ.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r3.anchor: بحيث يشمل حوادث الجنة وما يتجدد لأهلها من دون إنقطاع على ما نحو ما يحكي من بيان الحوادث الكونية في الجفر الجامع

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r4.claim: Another solution is that successive thousand-year sets are written and erased as each period ends.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r4.anchor: ليس دفعة واحدة بل دفعات بأن يبين فيه جملة من الأشياء كحوادث ألف سنة مثلا ثم تمحى عند تمام الألف

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r5.claim: This assumes the Tablet is a body with finite dimensions, so an unlimited record cannot be placed in it all at once in the ordinary sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r5.anchor: أن اللوح عند المسلمين جسم وكل جسم متناه الأبعاد كما تشهد به الأدلة وبيان كل شيء فيه على الوجه المعروف لنا دفعة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r6.claim: If the universal means this world's events, human deeds, and conditions, recording everything at once poses no difficulty.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r6.anchor: وأذا أريد بكل شيء الأشياء التي في هذه النشأة وأفعال العباد وأحوالهم فيها فلا إشكال في البيان على الوجه المعروف دفعة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r7.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the Tablet reading: it contains what occurred and will occur until Judgment, a finite span supported by some reports; unrestricted reports are read in light of restricted ones.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r7.anchor: والذي يترجح عندي أن ما كتب في اللوح ما كان وما يكون إلى يوم القيامة وهو متناه وبعض الآثار تشهد بذلك والمطلق منها محمول على المقيد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r8.claim: The Tablet's true nature is not decisively established, so al-Alusi avoids specifying it; reports of red ruby and green emerald sides are not certainly authentic.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r8.anchor: وحقيقة اللوح لم يرد فيها ما يفيد القطع ولذا تمسك عن تعيينها وكون أحد وجهيه ياقوتة حمراء والثاني زمردة خضراء جاء في بعض الآثار ولا جزم لنا بصحته

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r9.claim: Some interpret the imam as God's eternal knowledge, as they do Umm al-Kitab in 13:39, a foundation nothing possible can contradict.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r9.anchor: وفسر بعضهم الإمام المبين بعلمه تعالى الأزلي كما فسر أم الكتاب في قوله تعالى : ( وعنده أم الكتاب ) به

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r10.claim: On this reading mubīn means manifesting because knowledge discloses its object, or because creation follows knowledge and will.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r10.anchor: ووصفه بمبين لأنه مظهر فقد قالوا : العلم صفة يتجلى بها المذكور لمن قامت به أو لأن إظهار الأشياء

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r11.claim: Al-Alusi considers the eternal-knowledge interpretation a departure from the apparent sense; its deeper questions belong in kalam works.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r11.anchor: ولا يخفى ما في هذا التفسير من ارتكاب خلاف الظاهر وعليه فلا كلام في العموم نعم في كيفية وجود الأشياء في علمه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r12.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says the imam is records of deeds; al-Alusi says this is unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r12.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه أريد به صحف الأعمال وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r13.speaker: بعض غلاة الشيعة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r13.claim: Some extremist Shiʿis identify the imam as Ali, claiming all things are encompassed in him or that he stores knowledge like the Tablet; al-Alusi calls this ignorance.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r13.anchor: وحكى لي عن بعض غلاة الشيعة أن المراد بالإمام المبين علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وإحصاء كل شيء فيه من باب : ليس على الله بمستنكر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r14.claim: Al-Alusi suggests the claim might be excused if it intended the Sufi technical use of the clear book for the perfect human; he affirms Ali's excellence.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p219/r14.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال : إنهم أرادوا بذلك نحو ما أراده المتصوفة في إطلاقهم الكتاب المبين على الإنسان الكامل اصطلاحا منهم على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p220/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220/r1.speaker: أبو السمأل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220/r1.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads وكل in the nominative as the start of a nominal sentence.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمأل ( وكل ) بالرفع على الإبتداء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r1.claim: Moses heard God's speech directly, without intermediary but from behind a veil; people hear it from a human reciter's articulated voice, not immediately from God behind that person.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r1.anchor: موسى عليه السلام سمع من الله عزوجل بلا واسطة لكن من وراء حجاب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r2.claim: The Sunni formula that the uncreated Qur'an is recited by tongues, heard by ears, kept in hearts, and written in codices means it appears in created manifestations without residing in them, so its pre-eternity remains intact.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r2.anchor: القرآن كلام الله عزوجل غير مخلوق وهو مقروء بألسنتنا مسموع بآذاننا محفوظ في صدورنا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r3.claim: The eternal's manifestation in a created locus does not compromise its eternity or transcendence and does not entail indwelling, corporealism, or temporal events in God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r3.anchor: وهذا عين الدليل على أن تجلي القديم في مظهر حادث لا ينافي قدمه وتنزيهه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r4.claim: This account explains reports that the Qur'an appears as a pale man meeting its companion when the grave opens, and as an adversary against someone who carried it but violated it, or a defender of one who carried and preserved it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r4.anchor: وعنه يظهر معنى ظهور القرآن في صورة الرجل الشاحب يلقى صاحبه حين ينشق عنه القبر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r5.claim: With this framework, the author dismisses objections made by Ibn Taymiyya, Ibn al-Qayyim, Ibn Qudama, Ibn Qadi al-Jabal, al-Tufi, Abu Nasr, and others as polemical attacks by scholars whose reasoning sometimes erred.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r5.anchor: ورأى أن تشنيع إبن تيمية وإبن القيم وإبن قدامة وإبن قاضي الجبل والطوفي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r6.claim: He concludes that overlooking the faults of the great scholars is closer to piety and a mark of noble character, rather than answering their attacks in kind.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p18/r6.anchor: على أن العفو أقرب للتقوى والأغضاء مبني الفتوة وعليه الفتوى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p10/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p10/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p10/r1.claim: The Prophet says those who walk farther to prayer earn greater reward, and waiting to pray with the imam earns more than praying and then sleeping.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p10/r1.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أعظم الناس أجرا في الصلاة أبعدهم فأبعدهم ممشى والذي ينتظر الصلاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p10/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p10/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p10/r2.claim: To enumerate a thing means to preserve it, count it, and make it clear.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p10/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p10/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p10/r3.claim: The clear register is the Preserved Tablet.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r1.claim: Reviving the dead means resurrection, or guiding ignorant people.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r2.claim: What people sent ahead comprises their past good and evil deeds.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r2.anchor: ما أسلفوا من الأعمال الصالحة والطالحة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r3.claim: Good traces include knowledge taught and an endowment established; bad traces include spreading falsehood and founding injustice.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r4.claim: The clear register listing everything is the Preserved Tablet.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:12-13/r4.anchor: فى إمام مبين } يعني اللوح المحفوظ.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r1.claim: After establishing messengerhood and its glad tidings, the passage turns to resurrection, which helps affirm God's oneness and consoles believers who suffer in worldly life.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r1.anchor: الأصل الثاني هو الرسالة واتبعها ثمرتها المختومة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r2.claim: The emphatic plural of majesty announces the grandeur of these purposes and that only the Majestic can protect the small, distinct group of believers.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r3.claim: God revives the dead gradually in this life and all together at the Hour, physically through resurrection and spiritually by rescuing whom He wills from obscurity.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r3.anchor: أي بحسب التدريج الآن وجملة في الساعة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r4.claim: What people send ahead includes all their actions, states, and words, recorded together when the spirit is breathed.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r5.claim: Their آثار are the practices they leave behind, good or bad; each person is repaid for them in the unending afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r5.anchor: أي سنتهم التي تبقى من بعدهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r6.claim: To show that the record covers more than human deeds and that God needs no external aid, He says that He encompasses every created and uncreated matter in eternal knowledge and writing.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r7.claim: The clear Imam is a fitting book to consult, in which no circumstance is hidden from anyone seeking its knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r7.anchor: أي كتاب هو أهل لأن يقصد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r8.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by mutual implication: the verb implies enumeration, while Imam implies the act of writing.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p248/r8.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : دل فعل الإحصاء على مصدره وذكر الإمام على فعل الكتابة

DURR-FULL:v7p47/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r1.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r1.claim: Anas reports that Banū Salimah planned to sell their homes and move nearer the mosque; the Prophet asked whether they wanted their footsteps to be recorded, so they stayed.
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r1.anchor: عن أنس قال: أراد بنو سلمة أن يبيعوا دورهم ويتحولوا قريب المسجد

DURR-FULL:v7p47/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r2.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r2.claim: Anas says the recorded traces include footsteps taken on Friday.
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r2.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه في قوله {ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم} قال: هذا في الخطو يوم الجمعة

DURR-FULL:v7p47/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r3.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reports a distant worshipper refusing a donkey because he wanted his journeys and footsteps to the mosque counted; the Prophet promised him the full reward he sought.
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r3.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال: كان رجل ما يعلم من أهل المدينة ممن يصلي القبلة أبعد منزلا منه من المسجد

DURR-FULL:v7p47/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r4.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r4.claim: Abū Hurayrah reports that from leaving home to reaching a destination, a person gains a good deed and has a sin erased.
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من حين يخرج أحدكم من منزله

DURR-FULL:v7p47/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r5.speaker: مسروق
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r5.claim: Masrūq says every step is recorded by God as either a good or bad deed.
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r5.anchor: عن مسروق قال: ما خطا رجل خطوة إلا كتب الله له حسنة أو سيئة

DURR-FULL:v7p47/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r6.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r6.claim: The Prophet says those who live farther from the mosque receive greater reward.
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: الأبعد فالأبعد من المسجد أعظم أجرا

DURR-FULL:v7p47/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r7.claim: Mujāhid glosses what people send ahead as their deeds and their traces as the steps they take.
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {ونكتب ما قدموا} قال: أعمالهم {وآثارهم} قال: خطاهم بأرجلهم

DURR-FULL:v7p47/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r8.claim: Qatādah says God records every human trace and deed, even tracks the wind erases, whether done in obedience or disobedience; people should leave traces of obedience.
DURR-FULL:v7p47/r8.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في الآية قال: لو كان مغفلا شيئا من أثر ابن آدم لأغفل هذا الأثر

DURR-FULL:v7p48/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the traces include a practice people adopted after its founder's death.
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في قوله {ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم} قال: ما سنوا من سنة

DURR-FULL:v7p48/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r2.claim: Mujāhid explains what people send ahead as their good deeds and their traces as misguidance they leave behind.
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {ونكتب ما قدموا} قال: ما قدموا من خير {وآثارهم} قال: ما أورثوا من الضلالة

DURR-FULL:v7p48/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r3.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r3.claim: The Prophet says whoever establishes a good practice receives its reward and that of later followers; whoever establishes an evil practice bears its burden and theirs, with no reduction for either group.
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r3.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله البجلي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من سن سنة حسنة فله أجرها

DURR-FULL:v7p48/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r4.claim: Mujāhid identifies the clear register as the Mother of the Book.
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين} قال: أم الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v7p48/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r5.claim: Qatādah says everything is preserved with God in an Imam, meaning a book.
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين} قال: كل شيء من امام عند الله محفوظ

DURR-FULL:v7p48/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r6.claim: Ibrāhīm simply glosses the Imam as a book.
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r6.anchor: عن إبراهيم رضي الله عنه {وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين} قال: كتاب

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r1.claim: Abu Said reports that the Banu Salama, living far from the mosque, considered moving closer. After this verse was revealed, the Prophet told them their footsteps would be recorded, so they stayed where they were.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال : كانت بنو سلمة في ناحية من المدينة ، فارادوا ان ينتقلوا إلى قريب من المسجد

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r2.speaker: أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r2.claim: Anas explains the recorded traces as footsteps taken on Friday.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r2.anchor: عن انس رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : ونكتب ما قدموا واثارهم قال : هذا في الخطو يوم الجمعة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses what people sent ahead as their deeds and their traces as the steps made by their feet.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله ، عنه ونكتب ما قدموا قال : اعمالهم واثارهم قال : خطاهم بارجلهم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r4.claim: Qatada says God records every human deed and trace, including footprints erased by wind, whether made in obedience or disobedience; people should leave traces in obedience.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله ، عنه في الاية قال : لو كان مغفلا شيئا من اثر ابن ادم لاغفل هذا الاثر التي تعفها الرياح

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r5.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains the traces as a practice someone established and that others continued after his death.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : ونكتب ما قدموا واثارهم قال : ماسنوا من سنة فعملوا بها من بعد موتهم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r6.claim: Mujahid distinguishes prior deeds, which are good works, from traces, which are misguidance left as a legacy.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r6.anchor: مجاهد رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : نكتب ما قدموا قال : ما قدموا من خير واثارهم قال : ما اورثوا من الضلالة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r7.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله البجلي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r7.claim: The Prophet says whoever establishes a good practice earns its reward and the reward of those who follow it, and whoever establishes an evil practice bears its burden and theirs, without diminishing their shares; he then recited this verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r7.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله البجلي قال : ' قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : من سن سنة حسنة فله اجرها واجر من عمل بها من بعده

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r8.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r8.claim: The clear register is identified as the Mother of the Book.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3190/r8.anchor: وكل شيء احصيناه في امام مبين قال : أم الكتاب

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191/r1.claim: Qatada says everything is preserved with God in the clear register, meaning in a book.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191/r1.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : وكل شيء احصيناه في امام مبين قال : كل شيء من امام ، عند الله محفوظ ، يعني في كتاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r1.claim: Yā Sīn is Meccan by consensus, though a group treats the verse about deeds and traces as a Medinan exception concerning Banū Salima.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية بإجماع إلا أن فرقة قالت إن قوله، ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r2.claim: A group says the verse was revealed about Banū Salima, who wanted to leave their homes for the area beside the Prophet's mosque; the Prophet told them to remain because their footsteps were recorded and he disliked Madina being emptied.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r2.anchor: نزلت في بني سلمة من الأنصار حين أرادوا أن يتركوا ديارهم وينتقلوا إلى جوار مسجد رسول الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r3.claim: He rejects that occasion as the verse's revelation setting: it was revealed in Mecca, then invoked in Madina, where the Prophet's words matched its meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r3.anchor: وإنما نزلت الآية بمكة ولكنه احتج بها عليهم في المدينة ووافقها قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في المعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r4.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's saying that everything has a heart and Yā Sīn is the heart of the Qur'an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r4.anchor: وروى أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إن لكل شيء قلبا وإن قلب القرآن يس»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r5.speaker: عائشة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r5.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet said a sūra intercedes for its reciter and brings forgiveness to its listener, namely Yā Sīn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r5.anchor: وروت عائشة رضي الله عنها أنه عليه السلام قال: «إن في القرآن سورة يشفع قارئها ويغفر لمستمعها وهي يس»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r6.speaker: يحيى بن أبي كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r6.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr says that whoever recites Yā Sīn at night remains joyful until morning, a claim he says experience confirms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p445/r6.anchor: وقال يحيى بن أبي كثير: من قرأ سورة يس ليلا لم يزل في فرح حتى يصبح ويصدق ذلك التجربة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r1.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r1.claim: One group reads āthārahum in the accusative.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r2.speaker: مسروق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r2.claim: Masrūq reads āthārahum in the nominative.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو سعيد الخدري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī say the verse was revealed about Banū Salima's intended move beside the mosque; Ibn ʿAṭiyya refers back to his rejection of that setting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو سعيد الخدري إن هذه الآية نزلت في بني سلمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r4.claim: He says the Banū Salima revelation account has already been explained and rejected in the sūra's opening discussion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r4.anchor: وقد بينا ذلك في أول السورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r5.claim: Thābit al-Bunānī reports through Anas and Zayd that the Prophet stopped Zayd from hurrying to prayer and asked whether he knew that footsteps were recorded.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r5.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الصلاة فأسرعت في مشيي فحبسني، فلما انقضت الصلاة قال لي: يا زيد أما علمت أن الآثار تكتب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya identifies the preceding Prophetic report as an appeal to this verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r6.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: فهذا احتجاج بالآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r7.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r7.claim: Mujāhid, Qatāda, and al-Ḥasan interpret the traces as footsteps.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة والحسن: والآثار في هذه الآية الخطا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r8.speaker: أنس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r8.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits from Anas that the traces are the footsteps to Friday prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r8.anchor: وحكى الثعلبي عن أنس أنه قال: الآثار هي الخطا إلى الجمعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r9.claim: Another view takes traces as the lasting reputation of a deed that others follow: the originator receives their good-work reward or bears the burden of an evil practice.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r9.anchor: وقيل الآثار ما يبقى من ذكر العمل فيقتدى به فيكون للعامل أجر من عمل بسنته من بعده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r10.claim: The accusative kull is governed by an implied verb supplied by aḥṣaynāhu: the sense is that God recorded every thing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r10.anchor: وكل شيء نصب بفعل مضمر يدل عليه أحصيناه كأنه قال وأحصينا كل شيء أحصيناه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r11.claim: Imām means the authoritative book that is followed and serves as proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r11.anchor: و «الإمام» الكتاب المقتدى به الذي هو حجة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r12.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r12.claim: Mujāhid, Qatāda, and Ibn Zayd identify the clear register as the Preserved Tablet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r12.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد: أراد اللوح المحفوظ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r13.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448/r13.claim: Another group identifies the clear register as the records of deeds.

BURSEVI:v7p293#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p293#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p293#3/r10.claim: Kull shayʾ means absolutely everything, whether made by a human being or by someone else.
BURSEVI:v7p293#3/r10.anchor: من الأشياء كائنا ما كان سواء كان ما يصنعه الإنسان أو غيره

BURSEVI:v7p293#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p293#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p293#3/r11.claim: Kull shayʾ is governed by an implicit verb explained by aḥṣaynāhu, meaning that God recorded, bounded, and made it clear.
BURSEVI:v7p293#3/r11.anchor: وهو منصوب بفعل مضمر يفسره قوله :

BURSEVI:v7p294/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294/r1.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v7p294/r1.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says iḥṣāʾ originally means counting, then by metaphor came to mean clarification and preservation, since counting serves those ends.
BURSEVI:v7p294/r1.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : أصل الإحصاء العد ثم استعير للبيان والحفظ

BURSEVI:v7p294/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294/r2.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v7p294/r2.claim: Al-Raghib defines iḥṣāʾ as collecting by number; its name derives from pebbles, once used for counting as fingers are now.
BURSEVI:v7p294/r2.anchor: الإحصاء التحصيل بالعدد يقال : أحصيت كذا وذلك من لفظ الحصى

BURSEVI:v7p294/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p294/r3.claim: The manifest register is the Preserved Tablet, a great and comprehensive source manifesting everything past and future; it is called an imam because it is followed.
BURSEVI:v7p294/r3.anchor: أصل عظيم الشان مظهر لجميع الأشياء مما كان وما سيكون وهو اللوح المحفوظ سمي إماما لأنه يؤتم به ويتبع

BURSEVI:v7p294/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v7p294/r4.claim: Al-Raghib defines imam as something followed, such as a person, book, or other guide, whether rightly or wrongly; its plural is aʾimmah.
BURSEVI:v7p294/r4.anchor: قال الراغب : الإمام المؤتم به إنسانا كان يقتدي بقوله

BURSEVI:v7p294/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p294/r5.claim: The verse has also been interpreted as referring to the Preserved Tablet.
BURSEVI:v7p294/r5.anchor: فقد قيل : إشارة إلى اللوح المحفوظ

BURSEVI:v7p294/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p294/r6.claim: God's comprehensive recording both warns and encourages: knowing nothing escapes record should make a person watch every breath, movement, and stillness.
BURSEVI:v7p294/r6.anchor: وفي الإحصاء ترغيب وترهيب فإن المحصى لم يصح منه الغفلة في حال من الأحوال بل راقب نفسه في كل وقت

BURSEVI:v7p294/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p294/r7.claim: Reciting this divine name twenty times over each of twenty pieces of broken bread is said to subdue people's hearts.
BURSEVI:v7p294/r7.anchor: خاصية هذا الاسم تسخير القلوب فمن قرأه عشرين مرة على كل كسرة من الخبز والكسر عشرون

BURSEVI:v7p294/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p294/r8.claim: Subduing people can avert harm or bring benefit, especially through teaching and guidance, but some great Sufis leave influence to God's will; mastery of the lower self matters more than outward authority.
BURSEVI:v7p294/r8.anchor: واختار بعض الكبار ترك التصرف والالتفات إلى جانب الخلق بضرب من الحيل

BURSEVI:v7p294/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p294/r9.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya reads everything done to draw near to God as effects and lights inscribed in the Preserved Tablet of the beloveds' hearts.

BURSEVI:v7p294/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p294/r10.claim: The perfected human heart is a divine manifest tablet bearing lights of the unseen kingdom and imprinted mysteries of the realm of power, accessible after purification beyond ordinary human and rational capacities.
BURSEVI:v7p294/r10.anchor: واعلم أن قلب الإنسان الكامل اسم مبين ولوح إلهي فيه أنوار الملكوت منتقشة وأسرار الجبروت منطبعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r1.claim: God raises the dead for resurrection.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r2.claim: God records the good and evil people did in their worldly lives.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ ونكتب ما قدموا ﴾ من خير وشر في دنياهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r3.speaker: النخعي والجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r3.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī and al-Jaḥdarī read yuktab with yāʾ, passive morphology, and rafʿ on the verb and on āthāruhum.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r3.anchor: قرأ النخعي والجحدري ويكتب بياء مرفوعة وفتح التاء وآثارهم برفع الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r4.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r4.claim: One explanation of their traces is the footprints they leave; al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and Qatāda hold this view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r4.anchor: وفي أثارهم ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنها خطاهم بأرجلهم قاله الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r5.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports that Banū Salima complained of their distance from the mosque; the Prophet told them to stay, since their footsteps were recorded.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r5.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عليكم منازلكم فانما تكتب آثاركم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r6.speaker: قتادة وعمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r6.claim: Qatāda and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz say that if God overlooked nothing, He would not overlook what winds erase of a person’s footprints.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة وعمر بن عبد العزيز لو كان الله مغفلا شيئا لأغفل ما تعفي الرياح من أثر قدم ابن آدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r7.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r7.claim: Anas ibn Mālik explains the traces as footsteps taken to Friday prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r7.anchor: والثاني أنها الخطا إلى الجمعة قاله أنس بن مالك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr identify the traces as good or bad practices people establish and others continue; al-Farrāʾ, Ibn Qutayba, and al-Zajjāj prefer this reading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p8#3/r8.anchor: والثالث ما أثروا من سنة حسنة أو سيئة يعمل بها بعدهم قاله ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير واختاره الفراء وابن قتيبة والزجاج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r1.claim: What people sent ahead means the deeds they performed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {ونكتب ما قدموا} أي: من الأعمال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r2.claim: One interpretation of their آثار is the effects or practices people leave behind; they are recompensed for these as well as their own deeds, for good or evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r2.anchor: نكتب أعمالهم التي باشروها بأنفسهم، وآثارهم التي أثروها من بعدهم، فنجزيهم على ذلك أيضا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r3.claim: The Prophet says whoever introduces a good or bad practice in Islam receives its reward or burden and that of later followers, without reducing theirs; Muslim transmits it from Jarir ibn Abd Allah in the story of the Mudari people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r3.anchor: كقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من سن في الإسلام سنة حسنة، كان له أجرها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says that after a person dies, deeds cease except for useful knowledge, a righteous child who prays for them, or ongoing charity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا مات ابن آدم، انقطع عمله إلا من ثلاث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets the traces people leave as the misguidance they bequeathed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال: سمعت مجاهدا يقول في قوله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says traces are practices people initiate and others follow after their death; the initiator shares their followers' reward or burden without diminishing it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p565#2/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم} يعني: ما أثروا. يقول: ما سنوا من سنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r1.speaker: البغوي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r1.claim: Al-Baghawi chooses the interpretation of آثار as legacies people leave behind, including misguidance or practices followed after death.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r2.claim: The second interpretation is that آثار means the footprints people leave while moving toward obedience or sin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r2.anchor: والقول الثاني: أن المراد بذلك آثار خطاهم إلى الطاعة أو المعصية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r3.speaker: مجاهد، والحسن، وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r3.claim: Mujahid says what they sent ahead is their deeds and their آثار are their footsteps; al-Hasan and Qatada give the same explanation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r3.anchor: قال ابن أبي نجيح وغيره، عن مجاهد: {ما قدموا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r4.claim: Qatada says God records every trace and deed, including traces of obedience or sin; people should strive to leave traces in obedience.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: لو كان الله تعالى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r5.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r5.claim: When Banu Salima considered moving closer to the mosque, the Prophet told them to stay because their footsteps would be recorded; Muslim transmits the report from Jabir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r5.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: خلت البقاع حول المسجد، فأراد بنو سلمة أن ينتقلوا قرب المسجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r6.claim: A report from Abu Saʿid says Banu Salima wanted to move near the mosque, but the Prophet told them their traces were recorded and they stayed; al-Tirmidhi grades its Sufyan version hasan gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p566/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: كانت بنو سلمة في ناحية من المدينة، فأرادوا أن ينتقلوا إلى قريب من المسجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r1.claim: Al-Bazzar transmits from Abu Saʿid that Banu Salima complained of their distance from the mosque, the verse was revealed, and they stayed; another version raises the report to the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال: إن بني سلمة شكوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد منازلهم من المسجد، فنزلت: {ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r2.speaker: author
