IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir regards the claim that this verse was revealed over Banu Salima's mosque distance as strange because the whole surah is Meccan, and leaves the matter to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r2.anchor: وفيه غرابة من حيث ذكر نزول هذه الآية، والسورة بكمالها مكية، فالله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r3.claim: An unraised report from Ibn Abbas says the Ansar lived far from the mosque, wanted to move closer, then stayed after this verse was revealed; al-Tabarani gives a similar report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r3.anchor: ابن عباس قال: كانت منازل الأنصار متباعدة من المسجد، فأرادوا أن ينتقلوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r4.claim: The Prophet says a person who dies away from his birthplace has the distance from birthplace to the end of his trace measured for him in Paradise; al-Nasaʾi and Ibn Majah transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p567/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: توفي رجل بالمدينة، فصلى عليه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r1.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r1.claim: Anas reports that Zayd reminded him that even footsteps are recorded when Anas hurried while walking with him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r1.anchor: مشيت مع زيد بن ثابت فأسرعت المشي، فقال: يا أنس، أما شعرت أن الآثار تكتب؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r2.claim: Recording footsteps supports, by stronger reasoning, recording the exemplary traces people leave for others in good or evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r2.anchor: فإنه إذا كانت هذه الآثار تكتب، فلأن تكتب تلك التي فيها قدوة بهم من خير أو شر بطريق الأولى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r3.claim: All created things are recorded in a precise written register preserved in the Preserved Tablet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r3.anchor: جميع الكائنات مكتوب في كتاب مسطور مضبوط في لوح محفوظ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r4.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r4.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd identify the Clear Register here as the Mother of the Book.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r4.anchor: الإمام المبين هاهنا هو أم الكتاب. قاله مجاهد، وقتادة، وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r5.claim: In 17:71, each people is called with its record of deeds, which testifies to good and evil; 39:69 and 18:49 describe the opened record and its completeness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568/r5.anchor: أي: بكتاب أعمالهم الشاهد عليهم بما عملوه من خير وشر، كما قال تعالى

MUJAHID:v2p533#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p533#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p533#3/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses what people sent ahead as their deeds.
MUJAHID:v2p533#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ونكتب ما قدموا يعني أعمالهم

MUJAHID:v2p533#3/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p533#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p533#3/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses people's traces as their footsteps.
MUJAHID:v2p533#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ونكتب ما قدموا يعني أعمالهم ( وآثارهم ) يعني خطاهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r1.claim: God revives the dead either to raise them after death or to bring them from disbelief into faith.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r1.anchor: لبعثهم بعد مماتهم أو نخرجهم من الشرك إلى الإيمان

NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r2.claim: God records the good and other deeds people sent ahead.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r2.anchor: ما أسلفوا من الأعمال الصالحات وغيرها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r3.claim: Traces include lasting good legacies such as taught knowledge, books, endowments, lodgings, and mosques, and harmful practices they initiated; people bear these effects after death.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r3.anchor: ما هلكوا عنه من أثر حسن كعلم علموه أو كتاب صنفوه أو حبيس حبسوه أو رباط أو مسجد صنعوه أو سيىء كوظيفة وظفها بعض الظلمة وكذلك كل سنة حسنة أو سيئة يستن بها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r4.claim: The distinction resembles the verse saying a person will be told what he sent ahead and left behind.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r4.anchor: ونحوه قوله تعالى ينبأ الإنسان يومئذ بما قدم وآخر قدم من أعماله وأخر من آثاره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r5.claim: Another view takes traces to mean footsteps toward Friday or congregational prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r5.anchor: وقيل هى خطاهم إلى الجمعة أو إلى الجماعة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r6.claim: The clear register is the Preserved Tablet, source and model for other books; ahsayna means counted and made clear.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p4#5/r6.anchor: يعنى اللوح المحفوظ لأنه أصل الكتب ومقتداها

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r1.speaker: الضحاك والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Hasan interpret reviving the dead as giving life through faith after ignorance.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r1.anchor: وقال الضحاك والحسن: أي نحييهم بالإيمان بعد الجهل.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r2.claim: Qurtubi prefers resurrection for recompense, in reply to unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r2.anchor: والأول أظهر أي نحييهم بالبعث للجزاء

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r3.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r3.claim: They take what people send ahead as their deeds, which are recorded and counted.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: معناه من عمل. وقاله مجاهد وابن زيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r4.claim: He compares 82:5, 75:13, and 59:18 on what people send ahead or leave behind.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r4.anchor: ونظيره قوله: علمت نفس ما قدمت وأخرت

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r5.claim: Good traces bring posthumous reward: taught knowledge, books, endowed water, mosques, ribats, and bridges.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r5.anchor: من أثر حسن كعلم علموه، أو كتاب صنفوه، أو حبيس احتبسوه

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r6.claim: Evil traces include oppressive policies, harmful coinage, diversions from remembrance, and continued practices.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r6.anchor: أو سيىء كوظيفة وظفها بعض الظلام على المسلمين، وسكة أحدثها فيها تخسيرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r7.speaker: عمر وابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r7.claim: Another interpretation, adopted by ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbas, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr, is footsteps to mosques.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r7.anchor: وقيل: هي آثار المشائين إلى المساجد. وعلى هذا المعنى تأول الآية عمر وابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas also glosses traces as footsteps to mosques.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا أن معنى: «وآثارهم» خطاهم إلى المساجد.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r9.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r9.claim: Al-Nahhas prefers the footsteps interpretation because the Ansar lived far from the mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r9.anchor: قال النحاس: وهذا أولى ما قيل فيه لأنه قال: إن الآية نزلت في ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r10.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says a good deed is written and a bad one erased for each step to and from the mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12/r10.anchor: وفي الحديث مرفوعا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r1.claim: Jabir’s report in Muslim says the Prophet told Banu Salima to stay because their steps were recorded; they stayed.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r1.anchor: يا بني سلمة دياركم تكتب آثاركم

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r2.claim: Thabit reports Anas checked his hurried walk and cited the Prophet’s teaching that footsteps are recorded.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r2.anchor: وقال ثابت البناني: مشيت مع أنس بن مالك إلى الصلاة فأسرعت، فحبسني

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r3.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r3.claim: Qatada, Mujahid, and al-Hasan also interpret the traces as footsteps.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة ومجاهد أيضا والحسن: الآثار في هذه الآية الخطا.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r4.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r4.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi relates from Anas that traces are footsteps to Friday prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r4.anchor: وحكى الثعلبي عن أنس أنه قال: الآثار هي الخطا إلى الجمعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r5.claim: Athar has singular athar, also pronounced athar.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r6.claim: The reports support reward for a more distant mosque; Anas passed a new mosque for an old one, and others favor greater distance.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r6.anchor: فلو كان بجوار مسجد، فهل له أن يجاوزه إلى الأبعد؟ اختلف فيه فروي عن أنس

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r7.speaker: الحسن وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan and others disapprove leaving a nearby mosque; this is Malik’s position.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r7.anchor: وكره الحسن وغيره هذا وقال: لا يدع مسجدا قربه ويأتي غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r8.claim: Jurists hold two views on passing one’s local mosque to pray in the principal mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r8.anchor: وفي تخطي مسجده إلى المسجد الأعظم قولان.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r9.claim: Ibn Majah’s report from Anas gives rewards of one at home, 25 in a tribal mosque, and 500 in the congregational mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r9.anchor: وخرج ابن ماجه من حديث أنس بن مالك قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r10.claim: Diyārakum in the report is accusative as an exhortation: stay in your houses.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r11.claim: Naktub is jussive as the response to the command.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r12.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r12.claim: Kulla shayʾ may be accusative under an implied verb or nominative as subject; al-Khalil and Sibawayh prefer accusative.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r13.claim: An imam is a followed book and authoritative proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r13.anchor: والإمام: الكتاب المقتدى به الذي هو حجة.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r14.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r14.claim: They identify it as the Preserved Tablet.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r14.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد: أراد اللوح المحفوظ.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r15.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:36:12#2/r15.claim: Another group says it means the pages of deeds.

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r1.claim: After establishing the message, the passage states resurrection as another of the three principles that make a morally responsible person a believer and Muslim.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r1.anchor: لما بين الرسالة وهو أصل من الأصول الثلاثة التي يصير بها المكلف مؤمنا مسلما ذكر أصلا آخر وهو الحشر

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r2.claim: Because the full reward and punishment promised in the warning and glad tidings are not visible in worldly life, God will resurrect people and reward those warned and those given good news.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r2.anchor: فالله يحيي الموتى ويجزي المنذرين ويجزي المبشرين

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r3.claim: Resurrection is also offered as confirmation of the preceding description of fearing the All-Merciful unseen.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r3.anchor: لما ذكر خشية الرحمن بالغيب ذكر ما يؤكده وهو إحياء الموتى

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r4.claim: One parsing makes “We indeed” a subject and predicate, like a famous person identifying himself simply as “I”; God is known by his perfect attributes, so his self-identification suffices.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r4.anchor: أن يكون مبتدأ وخبرا كقول القائل

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, “We” is emphatic and “give life” is the predicate; al-Razi prefers this parsing.

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r6.claim: The phrase signals God's oneness: unlike people who need names and lineage to distinguish them from namesakes, God has no partner from whom he must be distinguished; thus message, oneness, and resurrection are all stated.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r6.anchor: ليس غيرنا أحد يشاركنا حتى تقول أنا كذا فنمتاز

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r7.claim: One reading takes “what they sent ahead” to include both what they did earlier and what they left for later, with one side of the pair stated alone, as in clothing that protects from heat while cold is also intended.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r7.anchor: فاكتفى بذكر أحدهما كما في قوله

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r8.claim: A second reading is the good or bad deeds they sent ahead into existence.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r8.anchor: المعنى ما أسلفوا من الأعمال صالحة كانت أو فاسدة

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#2/r9.claim: A third possibility is that what is recorded as sent ahead is their intentions, which precede their deeds, while their traces are the deeds themselves.

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r1.claim: The traces may be footprints: when Companions whose homes were far from mosques considered moving, the Prophet told them to remain, saying God records and rewards their steps.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r1.anchor: إن الله يكتب خطواتكم ويثيبكم عليه فالزموا بيوتكم

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r2.claim: Traces can also be lasting good practices (such as books, bridges, and charitable endowments) or bad practices (such as misleading books and instruments of vice), which bring reward or liability to their originators.

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r3.claim: The Prophet says whoever establishes a good practice receives its reward and the reward of those who follow it without reducing theirs, while whoever establishes an evil practice bears its burden and the burden of those who follow it.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r3.anchor: من سن سنة حسنة فله أجرها وأجر من عمل بها

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r4.claim: Another explanation identifies the traces as deeds and what was sent ahead as intentions, which come before deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r4.anchor: ما ذكرنا أن الآثار الأعمال وما قدموا النيات فإن النية قبل العمل

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r5.claim: Although writing precedes resurrection in time, resurrection is named first because it is the central purpose: without resurrection for reckoning, writing is not significant, and without revival the record has no effect.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r5.anchor: الكتابة معظمة لأمر الإحياء لأن الإحياء إن لم يكن للحساب لا يعظم والكتابة في نفسها إن لم تكن إحياء وإعادة لا يبقى لها أثر

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r6.claim: The emphatic “We indeed” conveys majesty; resurrection, God's uniquely great act, is therefore stated before the lesser act of writing, which further magnifies it.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r6.anchor: الإحياء عظيم يختص بالله والكتابة دونه فقرن بالتعريف الأمر العظيم

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r7.claim: One view says the record confirms that people's deeds and traces are fixed in advance: God first wrote what they would do, then records it when they do it.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r7.anchor: فإن القلم جف بما هو كائن

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r8.claim: Another view says the phrase assures preservation: unlike notes that can be lost, what God records is kept in a clear register.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r8.anchor: نكتب ونحفظ ذلك في إمام مبين

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r9.claim: A third view generalizes from deeds and traces to every thing: no word or act escapes God's knowledge or is lost from the record.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r9.anchor: شيئا من الأقوال والأفعال لا يعزب عن علم الله ولا يفوته

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r10.claim: “We enumerated it” is stronger than “We wrote it,” because scattered writing would still require collecting and totaling what was recorded.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r10.anchor: لأن من كتب شيئا مفرقا يحتاج إلى جمع عدده

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r11.claim: The register is called an imam because angels follow its instructions about lifespan, provision, revival, and death.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r11.anchor: وسمي الكتاب إماما لأن الملائكة يتبعونه فما كتب فيه من أجل ورزق وإحياء وإماتة اتبعوه

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r12.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r12.claim: An alternative identification of the clear register is the Preserved Tablet.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r12.anchor: وإمام جاء جمعا في قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r13.claim: “Imam” can be singular, like “book” and “veil,” or plural, like “mountains” and “ropes”; al-Razi reads the form in 17:71 as plural, “their leaders.”
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r13.anchor: فإمام إذا كان فردا فهو ككتاب وحجاب وإذا كان جمعا فهو كجبال وحبال

RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r14.claim: “Clear” means that the register manifests to angels what they must do and to people what will be done to them; it also distinguishes the creatures' outcomes, separating the people of Paradise from those of the Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v26p43#3/r14.anchor: والمبين هو المظهر للأمور لكونه مظهرا للملائكة ما يفعلون وللناس ما يفعل بهم وهو الفارق يفرق بين أحوال الخلق

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r1.claim: The verse follows the counsel to warn and leave disbelievers to their choices: their wrongdoing will be reckoned at the Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r1.anchor: the price of their wrongdoing will come due upon the Resurrection

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r2.claim: Giving life to the dead can refer to the Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r2.anchor: can be seen as a reference to the Resurrection

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r3.claim: IK reads giving life to the dead as God reviving the earth after its death.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r3.anchor: to God’s bringing the earth back to life, as in 57:17: Know that God revives the earth after its death (IK)

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r4.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r4.claim: Z reads it as God bringing people from idolatry to faith.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r4.anchor: bringing people from idolatry to faith (Z)

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r5.speaker: Aj, IK
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r5.claim: Aj and IK read it as reviving hearts deadened by heedlessness and ignorance through knowledge and truth.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r5.anchor: the revivification, through knowledge and truth, of hearts made dead through heedlessness and ignorance (Aj, IK)

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r6.claim: What people sent forth means deeds that will testify for or against them in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r6.anchor: refers to the deeds that will testify for or against them in the Hereafter

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r7.claim: What people leave behind literally means their footsteps or traces.

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r8.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r8.claim: The Banū Salimah, settled far from the mosque, wanted to move nearer; after the verse was revealed, the Prophet said their rewarded footprints were recorded and asked why they wished to move.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r8.anchor: So the Prophet said to them, “Your footprints are recorded

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r9.speaker: Aj, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r9.claim: Aj and Ṭ understand the traces more broadly as good deeds one leaves behind.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r9.anchor: the traces of good deeds that one leaves behind (Aj, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r10.speaker: ḥadīth
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r10.claim: A well-known hadith says the dead person’s deeds end except beneficial knowledge, a righteous child’s prayer, and ongoing charity left behind.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r10.anchor: As a well-known ḥadīth states, “When the son of Adam dies, all his deeds come to an end except three:

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r11.speaker: Aj, Ṭb, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r11.claim: Aj, Ṭb, and Ṭs read the clear registry as the Preserved Tablet, the leader of other books, containing God’s decrees.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r11.anchor: all things from the beginning of time to its end on the Preserved Tablet (85:22; Aj, Ṭb, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r12.speaker: Aj, IK, Q, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r12.claim: Aj, IK, Q, and Ṭs instead take the clear imam as the book or registry recording human actions.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r12.anchor: Others say imām refers to the book or “registry” in which all human actions are recorded (Aj, IK, Q, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r13.speaker: Shiite theologians
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r13.claim: Shiite theologians cite the verse as Quranic support for divinely ordained imamate after the Prophet’s death.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r13.anchor: cited by Shiite theologians as Quranic support for the Shiite understanding of Divinely ordained leadership

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r14.speaker: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r14.claim: Al-Qummī reports ʿAlī saying he is the clear imam who distinguishes truth from falsehood and inherited the office from the Messenger.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r14.anchor: al-Qummī relates a saying from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: “I, by God, am the clear imām

STUDYQURAN:36:12/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r15.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r15.claim: Shiite sources report the Prophet saying that ʿAlī is the Imam in whom God records knowledge of all things.
STUDYQURAN:36:12/r15.anchor: the Prophet said regarding ʿAlī,“He is the Imam in whom God records the knowledge of all things” (Qm, Ṭb)

TAB-FULL:v19p409/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p409/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p409/r1.claim: God revives the dead He created and records good and evil deeds people performed in worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v19p409/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إنا نحن نحيي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا} [يس: 12] من عمل

TAB-FULL:v19p409/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p409/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p409/r2.claim: Qatada glosses what people sent ahead as their deeds.
TAB-FULL:v19p409/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إنا نحن نحيي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا} [يس: 12] من عمل

TAB-FULL:v19p409/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p409/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v19p409/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses what people sent ahead as what they did.
TAB-FULL:v19p409/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله : {ونكتب ما قدموا} [يس: 12] قال: «ما عملوا»

TAB-FULL:v19p409/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p409/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v19p409/r4.claim: Mujahid glosses what people sent ahead as their deeds.

TAB-FULL:v19p410/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r1.claim: Their آثار are traces of their footsteps.
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r1.anchor: عن جابر، قال: أراد بنو سلمة قرب المسجد، قال: فقال لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يا بني سلمة» دياركم، إنها تكتب آثاركم

TAB-FULL:v19p410/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Ansar lived far from the mosque and stayed in place after the verse when they considered moving closer.
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " كانت منازل الأنصار متباعدة من المسجد، فأرادوا أن ينتقلوا إلى المسجد

TAB-FULL:v19p410/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r3.speaker: جابر
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r3.claim: Jabir reports that Banu Salima wanted to move closer, but the Prophet told them to stay because their footsteps were recorded.
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r3.anchor: عن جابر، قال: أراد بنو سلمة قرب المسجد، قال: فقال لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يا بني سلمة» دياركم، إنها تكتب آثاركم

TAB-FULL:v19p410/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r4.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that Banu Salima complained about the distance; the verse came down and they were told to stay because their footsteps were recorded.
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r4.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، قال: شكت بنو سلمة بعد منازلهم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فنزلت: {إنا نحن نحيي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم} [يس: 12]

TAB-FULL:v19p410/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r5.speaker: ثابت
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r5.claim: Thabit recounts that Anas remembered Zayd ibn Thabit telling him that footsteps are recorded after Anas hurried to prayer.
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r5.anchor: عن ثابت، قال: مشيت مع أنس، فأسرعت المشي، فأخذ بيدي، فمشينا رويدا، فلما قضينا الصلاة قال أنس:

TAB-FULL:v19p410/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r6.claim: Al-Hasan reports that Banu Salima stayed in their distant homes after the Prophet told them to count their footsteps as reward.
TAB-FULL:v19p410/r6.anchor: عن الحسن، أن بني سلمة، كانت دورهم قاصية عن المسجد، فهموا أن يتحولوا، قرب المسجد، فيشهدون الصلاة مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v19p411/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p411/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p411/r1.claim: Their آثار refers to footsteps left on the ground.
TAB-FULL:v19p411/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله {ما قدموا وآثارهم} [يس: 12] قال: «خطاهم بأرجلهم»

TAB-FULL:v19p411/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p411/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v19p411/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله {ما قدموا وآثارهم} [يس: 12] قال: «خطاهم بأرجلهم»

TAB-FULL:v19p411/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p411/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v19p411/r3.claim: Al-Hasan's gloss, transmitted by Qatada, is that the traces mean footsteps.
TAB-FULL:v19p411/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {وآثارهم} [يس: 12] قال: قال الحسن: {وآثارهم} [يس: 12] قال: «خطاهم»

TAB-FULL:v19p411/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p411/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p411/r4.claim: Qatada says that if anything were overlooked in a person's affairs, it would be footprints erased by the wind.
TAB-FULL:v19p411/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: لو كان مغفلا شيئا من شأنك يا ابن آدم أغفل ما تعفي الرياح من هذه الآثار

TAB-FULL:v19p412/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r1.claim: Everything past and future is recorded in the Mother of the Book, the Clear Register.
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد {في إمام مبين} [يس: 12] قال: «في أم الكتاب»

TAB-FULL:v19p412/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r2.claim: The Register is called clear because it reveals the truth of everything recorded in it.
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد {في إمام مبين} [يس: 12] قال: «في أم الكتاب»

TAB-FULL:v19p412/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the Clear Register as the Mother of the Book.
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد {في إمام مبين} [يس: 12] قال: «في أم الكتاب»

TAB-FULL:v19p412/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r4.claim: Qatada says everything is recorded with God in a book.
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين} [يس: 12] «كل شيء محصى عند الله في كتاب»

TAB-FULL:v19p412/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v19p412/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Mother of the Book with God contains everything and is the Clear Register.

SULAMI:v2p171#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p171#5/r1.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
SULAMI:v2p171#5/r1.claim: God revives dead souls through success in service, dead hearts through the lights of faith, dead secrets through disclosure, and dead inmost hearts through witnessing.
SULAMI:v2p171#5/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن علي الترمذي في هذه الآية : إنا نحن نحيي الأنفس الميتة بتوفيق الخدمة

TABATABAI:36:12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:12/r2.claim: Reviving the dead refers to bringing them back to life for recompense.

TABATABAI:36:12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:12/r3.claim: What people send ahead is the work they performed before death.
TABATABAI:36:12/r3.anchor: والمراد بما قدموا الأعمال التي عملوها قبل الوفاة فقدموها على موتهم

TABATABAI:36:12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:12/r4.claim: Their traces are good or bad effects left after death: beneficial knowledge, a mosque, or ablution facility, and innovations or places of vice used for disobedience.
TABATABAI:36:12/r4.anchor: ما تركوها لما بعد موتهم من خير يعمل به كتعليم علم ينتفع به أو بناء مسجد يصلى فيه

TABATABAI:36:12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:36:12/r5.claim: A reported alternative makes what was sent ahead the intentions and the traces their resulting actions; the author considers this far from the context.
TABATABAI:36:12/r5.anchor: وربما قيل إن المراد بما قدموا النيات وبآثارهم الأعمال المترتبة المتفرعة عليها وهو بعيد من السياق

TABATABAI:36:12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:12/r6.claim: Writing deeds and traces means recording them in individual deed-books through the angel scribes, distinct from their enumeration in the clear Imam.
TABATABAI:36:12/r6.anchor: ثبتها في صحائف أعمالهم وضبطها فيها بواسطة كتبة الأعمال من الملائكة وهذه الكتابة غير كتابة الأعمال وإحصائها في الإمام المبين

TABATABAI:36:12/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:12/r7.claim: The author rejects identifying the writing of deeds and traces with their enumeration in the clear book: scripture distinguishes the universal register, each nation’s book, and each person’s record, and here contrasts writing with enumeration.
TABATABAI:36:12/r7.anchor: وظاهر الآية أيضا يقضي بنوع من البينونة بين كتاب الأعمال والإمام المبين حيث فرق بينهما بالخصوص والعموم واختلاف التعبير بالكتابة والإحصاء

TABATABAI:36:12/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:12/r8.claim: The clear Imam is the Preserved Tablet, unchanged, containing the detail of God’s decree for creation and enumerating everything; its several scriptural names each reflect a distinct aspect.
TABATABAI:36:12/r8.anchor: هو اللوح المحفوظ من التغيير الذي يشتمل على تفصيل قضائه سبحانه في خلقه فيحصي كل شيء

TABATABAI:36:12/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:12/r9.claim: It is called an Imam because its inexorable decree is followed by creation; deed-books are copied from it.
TABATABAI:36:12/r9.anchor: أنه لاشتماله على القضاء المحتوم متبوع للخلق مقتدى لهم وكتب الأعمال كما سيأتي في تفسير سورة الجاثية مستنسخة منه

TABATABAI:36:12#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r2.claim: The author rejects mapping the passage piecemeal onto the stories of Abu Jahl’s group and the distant Ansar homes: doing so disrupts the unified flow describing two responses to the call.
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r2.anchor: سياق الآيات يأبى الانطباق على هذه الروايات بما فيها من القصة فهو سياق متناسق منسجم يصف حال طائفتين من الناس

TABATABAI:36:12#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r3.claim: He argues that the verses came down together as one coherent passage: people divide into two groups when the call and warning reach them. This does not preclude an actual episode in which the Prophet was concealed from enemies.
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r3.anchor: فالحق أن الآيات نازلة دفعة ذات سياق واحد تصف حال الناس وتفرقهم عند بلوغ الدعوة ووقوع الإنذار على فرقتين، ولا مانع من وقوع القصة

TABATABAI:36:12#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r4.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports that Banu Salama wanted to move nearer the mosque; the Prophet called them, said their footsteps would be recorded, recited the verse, and they stayed. Al-Tirmidhī graded it ḥasan and al-Ḥākim authenticated it.
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال كان بنو سلمة في ناحية من المدينة فأرادوا أن ينتقلوا إلى قرب المسجد

TABATABAI:36:12#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the distant homes of the Anṣār led them to consider moving nearer the mosque; the verse came down and they chose to remain. No grading is stated.
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كانت الأنصار منازلهم بعيدة من المسجد فأرادوا أن ينتقلوا قريبا من المسجد فنزلت

TABATABAI:36:12#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r6.claim: The author says the two relocation reports have the same contextual difficulty as the earlier reports tying separate verses to the concealment story.
TABATABAI:36:12#2/r6.anchor: أقول والكلام في الروايتين كالكلام فيما تقدمهما

TABATABAI:36:12#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r1.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله البجلي
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r1.claim: The Prophet tells Jarīr that whoever starts a good practice earns its reward and followers’ rewards, while one who starts an evil practice bears its sin and followers’ sins; he then recites this verse.
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r1.anchor: من سن سنة حسنة فله أجرها وأجر من عمل بها من بعده من غير أن ينقص من أجورهم شيء

TABATABAI:36:12#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r2.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r2.claim: Al-Qummī’s commentary identifies the clear Imam as a clear, firmly established book.
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r2.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين } أي في كتاب مبين وهو محكم

TABATABAI:36:12#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r3.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports ʿAlī saying, ‘By God, I am the clear Imam’: he clarifies truth from falsehood and inherited it from the Prophet.
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r3.anchor: وذكر ابن عباس عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام أنا والله الإمام المبين أبين الحق من الباطل ورثته من رسول الله

TABATABAI:36:12#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r4.claim: A report in Maʿānī al-akhbār, through Abū al-Jārūd from Abū Jaʿfar and his forefathers, says of ʿAlī that he is the Imam in whom God gathered knowledge of everything.
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r4.anchor: في معاني الأخبار بإسناده إلى أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عن أبيه عن جده عليهم السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في حديث أنه قال في علي عليه السلام

TABATABAI:36:12#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r5.claim: If sound, the two reports about ʿAlī are inner Qur’anic allusions rather than exoteric tafsir; God may grant His uniquely devoted servant knowledge of the clear Book, and ʿAlī is the foremost monotheist after the Prophet.
TABATABAI:36:12#3/r5.anchor: لو صحا لم يكونا من التفسير في شيء بل مضمونهما من بطن القرآن وإشاراته

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364/r1.claim: What people send ahead is their deeds; their traces are the practices they establish for others to follow.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364/r1.anchor: ونكتب ما قدموا} من أعمالهم؛ {وآثارهم} ما استن به بعدهم من سننهم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364/r2.claim: He compares the phrase to 75:13, which speaks of what a person sent ahead and left behind as a lasting trace.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364/r2.anchor: وهو مثل قوله: {ينبأ الإنسان يومئذ بما قدم وأخر} (1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains reviving the dead as resurrection.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r2.claim: Muqātil says what people sent ahead includes good and evil deeds and what later people followed from them; al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj choose this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: من خير أو شر فاقتدى بها (¬2) من بعدهم. وهذا اختيار الفراء والزجاج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r3.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says their traces are practices they instituted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r3.anchor: وهو قول سعيد بن جبير، قال: {وآثارهم}: ما سنوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r4.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ’s transmission, Ibn ʿAbbās explains traces as the good or evil legacy someone leaves, as in 75:13.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: ما آثروا من أثر خير أو شر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r5.speaker: أنس وابن عباس في رواية عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r5.claim: Anas and Ibn ʿAbbās, in ʿIkrima’s transmission, report that the verse was revealed about Banū Salima, who considered moving closer to the Prophet’s mosque but stayed after its revelation; traces here are their footsteps.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r5.anchor: وقال أنس وابن عباس في رواية عكرمة: نزلت هذه الآية في بني سلمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r6.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan also explains their traces as their footsteps.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r6.anchor: وهو قول الحسن (¬1)، ومجاهد في رواية ابن أبي نجيح (¬2)، وقتادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r7.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن أبي نجيح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r7.claim: Mujāhid, in Ibn Abī Najīḥ’s transmission, also explains their traces as their footsteps.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r7.anchor: وهو قول الحسن (¬1)، ومجاهد في رواية ابن أبي نجيح (¬2)، وقتادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r8.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r8.claim: Qatāda also explains their traces as their footsteps.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r8.anchor: وهو قول الحسن (¬1)، ومجاهد في رواية ابن أبي نجيح (¬2)، وقتادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r9.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r9.claim: ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz says that if God were to leave any human trace unrecorded, it would be the trace winds rub away.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r9.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز: لو كان الله تاركا لابن آدم شيئا لترك ما عبث (¬4) عليه الرياح من أثر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r10.speaker: مسروق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r10.claim: Masrūq says every step a person takes is recorded as either a good deed or a sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r10.anchor: وقال مسروق: ما خطأ رجل خطوة إلا كتب حسنة أو سيئة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r11.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r11.claim: Mujāhid says what they sent ahead is good, while their traces are the misguidance and practice of error they leave behind.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p460/r11.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد قال: ما قدموا من خير، وآثارهم: وما أورثوا من الضلالة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says readers agree on the accusative kull because the verb’s object pronoun refers back to it; a nominative is also possible as a new sentence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: القراء يجمعون على نصب كل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ compares the accusative construction to “I struck Zayd and spoke to ʿAmr,” where the later noun remains accusative after the preceding verb; here too a verb precedes it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r2.anchor: والاختيار أن يقول: (¬2) ضربت زيدا وعمرا كلمته، ينتصب عمرا لسبق الفعل قبله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows nominative kull if the phrase is treated as a fresh sentence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r3.anchor: وهو قوله: {ونكتب ما قدموا}. ويجوز الرفع على الاستئناف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r4.claim: Muqātil says God made clear every deed that He recorded.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: {وكل شيء} من الأعمال ما (¬4) {أحصيناه} بيناه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses aḥṣaynāhu as “We preserved it.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r6.claim: Iḥṣāʾ means counting, and counting can mean either making something clear or preserving it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r6.anchor: ومعنى الإحصاء في اللغة: العد، والعد يكون للبيان ويكون للحفظ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r7.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil identify the clear register as the Preserved Tablet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: في اللوح المحفوظ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r8.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r8.claim: Mujāhid identifies it as the Mother of the Book.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r9.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r9.claim: The scholars of meaning say this register lets the angels compare it with events as they occur and demonstrates God’s detailed knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p461/r9.anchor: قال أهل المعاني (¬9): وفي ذلك اعتبار الملائكة إذ قابلوا به ما يحدث # من الأمور

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r1.claim: What people have sent ahead includes all the good and evil they have done.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r1.anchor: {ما قدموا} [يس: 12] ما عملوا من خير وشر، {وآثارهم}

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r2.claim: Their traces include a good practice they leave and others follow: they receive the followers’ reward without diminishing it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r2.anchor: {وآثارهم} [يس: 12] ما أخروا من سنة حسنة، فعمل بها بعدهم فلهم مثل أجر من عمل بها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r3.claim: Their traces also include an evil practice they leave and others follow: they bear the followers’ sin without diminishing it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r3.anchor: أو سنة سيئة فعمل بها بعدهم فإن عليه مثل وزر من عمل بها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r4.claim: Al-Hasan reports the Prophet saying that whoever calls to followed guidance receives the follower’s reward without loss, while whoever calls to followed error bears the follower’s sin without loss.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r4.anchor: أبو الأشهب، عن الحسن، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أيما داع دعا على هدى، فاتبع،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r5.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r5.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz explains their traces as their footsteps.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r5.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، عن عمر بن عبد العزيز، قال: {وآثارهم} [يس: 12] خطوهم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r6.claim: Qatada says that if God were to overlook anything about a person, it would be footprints that winds erase.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r6.anchor: قال قتادة: لو كان الله مغفلا شيئا، أي: تاركا شيئا من شأنك يابن آدم لا يحصيه لأغفل هذه الآثار

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r7.speaker: مسروق
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r7.claim: Masruq says every step a person takes is recorded as either a good deed or a sin.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r7.anchor: سفيان بن سعيد الثوري، عن الأعمش، عن أبي الضحى، عن مسروق قال: ما خطا عبد خطوة إلا كتب له حسنة أو سيئة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r8.claim: The clear register is a book.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p802#2/r8.anchor: قال: {وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين} [يس: 12] ، أي: في كتاب.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p254#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p254#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p254#2/r3.claim: In وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين, imam means a book or the Preserved Tablet.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p254#2/r3.anchor: وقال: وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين [يس: 12] يعني:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r1.claim: The verse cluster consoles the Prophet and believers under severe polytheist pressure, closing by stressing God's unmatched power and knowledge: only He resurrects the dead and knows every deed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r1.anchor: Müşriklerin ağır baskıları altında büyük sıkıntılar çeken Hz. Peygamber ve müminler için teselli ve moral kaynağı özelliği taşıyan bu âyet kümesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r2.speaker: Bazı ilk dönem müfessirleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r2.claim: Some early exegetes take “raising the dead” as bringing people out of polytheism into faith; the commentary cites al-Zamakhshari for this view.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r2.anchor: Bazı ilk dönem müfessirleri bu âyetteki “ölüleri diriltme” ifadesinden maksadın şirkten çıkarıp imana eriştirmek olduğunu belirtmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r3.claim: Since God already knows all that will happen in His eternal knowledge, recording human deeds meets no divine need; it helps people keep life's purpose and each action consciously in view.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r3.anchor: İnsanın bütün eylemlerinin kayda geçirilmesine yüce Allah’ın ihtiyacı yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r4.claim: This belief makes moral duty a concrete awareness that permeates life and guides every action, rather than leaving people with an abstract ethical obligation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r4.anchor: soyut bir ahlâkî görev telakkisiyle baş başa kalmamış olur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r5.claim: It teaches that a person's relation to the metaphysical is not confined to prayer and prescribed duties, and helps explain the close tie between physical events and transcendent realities.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r5.anchor: fizik âlemde olup bitenlerle fizik ötesi gerçekler arasındaki sıkı bağı kavramasını kolaylaştırır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r6.speaker: Zemahşerî ve Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and al-Shawkani explain that the phrase covers every deed, good or bad, and continuing effects that are entered as positive or negative entries in a person's record.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r6.anchor: olumlu veya olumsuz puanlar halinde kaydedildiği üzerinde durulur (Zemahşerî, III, 281; Şevkânî, IV, 414)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r7.claim: Useful knowledge taught or written, endowments, and helpful lasting buildings continue adding positive entries while their benefits persist.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r7.anchor: bir imkânını vakfedip kalıcı hayır yapma, insanların faydalanacakları hizmet binası

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r8.claim: Harmful practices, including those imposed by oppressive rulers, leave negative entries and increase liability after death when they make people suffer, lose property, or stray from God's way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r8.anchor: insanların eziyet çekmesine, zarara girmesine veya Allah yolundan sapmasına sebep olacak usuller ihdas etmek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r9.claim: The phrase may also be rendered as what people completed before death together with all their deeds whose traces continue.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r9.anchor: ölmeden yapıp tükettikleri, bitirdikleri ile izi ve eseri devam eden bütün işlerini (amellerini)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r10.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r10.claim: The Prophet says that after death the deed record closes except for ongoing charity, knowledge that continues to benefit, and a righteous child who prays for the deceased (Muslim; al-Tirmidhi).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r10.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in şu meâldeki hadisi insanların yararı devam ettiği sürece sevabı da yenilenen hayır faaliyetlerine yoğun biçimde yönelmelerinde ve özellikle vakıf kurumunun gelişmesinde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r11.claim: The hadith strongly encouraged people to pursue good works whose rewards continue through lasting benefit, especially helping the waqf institution develop.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r11.anchor: insanların yararı devam ettiği sürece sevabı da yenilenen hayır faaliyetlerine yoğun biçimde yönelmelerinde ve özellikle vakıf kurumunun gelişmesinde çok etkili olmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r12.claim: The hadith's statement that the deed record closes refers only to the recording of rewards; the verse also covers those whose harmful influence continues after death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r12.anchor: Fakat bu hadiste amel defterinin kapanması sevapların yazılması açısındandır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r13.speaker: Peygamber efendimiz
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r13.claim: The Prophet says that whoever initiates a good practice receives its reward and the reward of later followers, while whoever initiates an evil practice bears its sin and their sins (Muslim; Musnad).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r13.anchor: Peygamber efendimiz şu hadisinde başkalarını etkileyecek çığır açmanın iki şeklini de ayrı ayrı ifade etmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r14.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r14.claim: Ibn Atiyya lists explanations of imām as an authoritative book to be followed, the Preserved Tablet, or the books of deeds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r14.anchor: “levh-i mahfûz” ve “amel defterleri” gibi mânalarla açıklanmıştır (İbn Atıyye, IV, 448)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r15.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r15.claim: Ibn Ashur explains that calling God's knowledge imām, a guide or authority, indicates that everything connected with divine will and power unfolds in accordance with it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r15.anchor: bu kelimeyle nitelemesi, rabbânî irade ve kudretin ilişkili olduğu her şeyin ona uygun biçimde cereyan ettiğini belirtmek içindir (İbn Âşûr

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r16.speaker: Resûlullah
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r16.claim: When the Ansar clan of Banu Salama wanted to move closer to the Prophet's Mosque, he disapproved and told them that the traces of their steps would be recorded where they lived.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r16.anchor: Resûlullah bunu uygun görmemiş ve onlara “Kendi bulunduğunuz yerde de yaptıklarınızın izleri kayda geçirilir” buyurmuştu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r17.speaker: Bazıları
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r17.claim: Some cite the Banu Salama incident as evidence that this verse was revealed in Medina.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r17.anchor: Bazıları bu olayı delil göstererek bu âyetin Medine’de indiğini ileri sürmüşlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r18.claim: The Prophet's use of the verse's wording during an event in Medina does not prove that the verse itself was revealed there.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:12/r18.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in bu âyetteki ifadeyi Medine’de geçen olayda kullanmış olması onun Medine’de indiğini göstermez

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p364/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p364/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p364/r1.claim: Banu Salima wanted to move closer to the mosque; the Prophet told them their footsteps were recorded and advised them to keep their homes, and the report says the verse was revealed about this.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p364/r1.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخدري: كان بنو سلمة في ناحية من المدينة، فأرادوا أن ينتقلوا إلى قرب المسجد

DAMGHANI:v1p43/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p43/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p43/r6.claim: The إمام in which everything is recorded is a book, namely the Preserved Tablet.
DAMGHANI:v1p43/r6.anchor: الثالث : إمام يعني اللوح المحفوظ . قوله تعالى في سورة يس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines an imam as one followed, whose actions are imitated and whose aim is pursued; he relates it to intending.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج : الإمام : الذي يؤتم به ، ويفعل كفعله ، ويقصد ما قصده

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r2.claim: One sense is a person who precedes others in good and is followed as an example.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r2.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الإمام في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r3.claim: A second sense is a book, as in the account that people are summoned with their books.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الإمام في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r4.claim: An alternative interpretation of imam in that verse is each person's prophet.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r5.claim: A third sense is the Preserved Tablet; the source applies it to the record of all things in this verse.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الإمام في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r6.claim: A fourth sense is a road or path.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الإمام في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r7.claim: Ibn Qutaybah says a road is called an imam because travelers follow it for guidance; imam originally means what one follows.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p126/r7.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : وإنما سمي الطريق إماما لأن المسافر يأتم به ويستدل . وأصل الإمام ما ائتممت به

BURSEVI:v7p294#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p294#2/r1.claim: Purification removes what is merely imagined so the realized truth can appear; failing to distinguish illusion from reality deprives one of the real.
BURSEVI:v7p294#2/r1.anchor: ومعنى التصفية إزالة المتوهم ليظهر المتحقق فمن لم يدر المتوهم من المتحقق حرم من المتحقق

BURSEVI:v7p294#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294#2/r2.speaker: الجامي
BURSEVI:v7p294#2/r2.claim: Al-Jami's dog mistakes a bone's reflection in clear water for another bone, drops the bone in its mouth, and loses the real one by pursuing the unreal image.
BURSEVI:v7p294#2/r2.anchor: برد بياره سك كمان كه مكر هست در آب استخوان دكر لب وبكشاد سوى آن بستاد استخوان ازدهان در آب فتاد

BURSEVI:v7p294#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p294#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p294#2/r3.claim: The spiritual lesson is to polish the mirror so the truth and reality of existence appear, yielding complete vision and witnessing.
BURSEVI:v7p294#2/r3.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يجلو المرآة ليظهر صورة الحقيقة وحقيقة الوجود ويحصل كمال العيان والشهود

TABRISI:36:14/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:14/r10.claim: Kulla shay'in is accusative under an understood verb, aḥṣaynā, which the explicit aḥṣaynāhu explains.
TABRISI:36:14/r10.anchor: { وكل شيء } منصوب بفعل مضمر يفسره هذا الظاهر

TABRISI:36:14/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14/r15.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
TABRISI:36:14/r15.claim: Mujahid and Qatada take what people sent ahead to be their obedience and sins in worldly life.
TABRISI:36:14/r15.anchor: من طاعتهم ومعاصيهم في دار الدنيا عن مجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:36:14/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14/r16.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:36:14/r16.claim: Al-Jubba'i reads their آثار as deeds that leave a continuing effect, in contrast to the acts they sent ahead.
TABRISI:36:14/r16.anchor: أي ما يكون له أثر عن الجبائي

TABRISI:36:14/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:14/r17.claim: Another explanation is deeds people establish as a precedent after their death, whether good or bad, and others follow them in it.
TABRISI:36:14/r17.anchor: وقيل: يعني بآثارهم أعمالهم التي صارت سنة بعدهم يقتدى فيها بهم

TABRISI:36:14/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14/r18.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
TABRISI:36:14/r18.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that Banu Salima, living far from the mosque, complained to the Prophet about the distance; the verse was then revealed regarding their footsteps to prayer.
TABRISI:36:14/r18.anchor: ما رواه أبو سعيد الخدري أن بني سلمة كانوا في ناحية المدينة فشكوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:36:14-19/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14-19/r1.speaker: أبو موسى
TABRISI:36:14-19/r1.claim: Abu Musa transmits the Prophet saying that those who walk the farthest to prayer receive the greatest reward; al-Bukhari and Muslim include the report in their Sahih collections.
TABRISI:36:14-19/r1.anchor: إن أعظم الناس أجرا في الصلاة أبعدهم إليها ممشى فأبعدهم

TABRISI:36:14-19/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14-19/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:14-19/r2.claim: The Imam Mubin is the Preserved Tablet, a manifest register of all events, allowing angels to compare it with what happens and demonstrating God's detailed knowledge.
TABRISI:36:14-19/r2.anchor: أي وأحصينا وعددنا كل شيء من الحوادث في كتاب ظاهر وهو اللوح المحفوظ

TABRISI:36:14-19/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14-19/r3.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:36:14-19/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says it means the records of deeds, called clear because their marks do not wear away.
TABRISI:36:14-19/r3.anchor: وقيل: أراد به صحائف الأعمال وسمي ذلك مبينا لأنه لا يدرس أثره عن الحسن

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r1.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the clear register as the Preserved Tablet.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r1.anchor: {مبين} بين، يعني: اللوح المحفوظ، وهو تفسير السدي

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that God first created the Pen and commanded it to write all that would happen through Resurrection; people's deeds are presented every Monday and Thursday and match the written record.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r2.anchor: نعيم بن يحيى، عن الأعمش، عن أبي ظبيان، عن ابن عباس، قال: أول ما خلق الله القلم، فقال: اكتب فقال: رب ما أكتب؟

ITQAN:v1p52/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p52/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد
ITQAN:v1p52/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim report from Abu Sa‘id that Banu Salama wanted to move nearer the mosque; the verse descended, and the Prophet said their footsteps were recorded, so they stayed.
ITQAN:v1p52/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال كانت بنو سلمة في ناحية المدينة

ITQAN:v2p383/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p383/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p383/r8.claim: Imām means a book or register.

FARRA:v2p373#2/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p373#2/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p373#2/r1.claim: All readers put kull in the accusative because the verb acts on its resumptive pronoun; nominative is also good, since kull with negation behaves like an indefinite, meaning nothing escaped recording.
FARRA:v2p373#2/r1.anchor: القراء مجتمعون على نصب (كل) لما وقع من الفعل على راجع ذكرها

MAJAZ:v2p158/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p158/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p158/r1.claim: Aḥṣaynāhu means We made it or recorded it.

MAJAZ:v2p158/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p158/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p158/r2.claim: The clear register is a clear book.
MAJAZ:v2p158/r2.anchor: «في إمام مبين» (12) أي فى كتاب مبين..

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r1.claim: The record of what people send ahead and leave behind includes both afterlife deeds and worldly acts or acts done for those who come after them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r1.anchor: both these types of deeds are being noted by God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r2.claim: Imām means leader, guide, and fountainhead; by extension it names a Book that guides and serves as a source, as with the Torah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r2.anchor: The actual meaning of the word امَمِإِ is “leader, guide and fountainhead.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r3.claim: Here imām is the central register recording everyone's deeds for reward or punishment, further affirming that no word or deed escapes God's record.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r3.anchor: it refers to the central register which records the deeds of all people

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p9/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p9/r1.speaker: ابن السميفع وابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p9/r1.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfi and Ibn Abi Abla read kull with the lām in the nominative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p9/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع وابن أبي عبلة وكل برفع اللام أي من الأعمال أحصيناه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p9/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p9/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p9/r2.claim: The clear register in which deeds are recorded is the Preserved Tablet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p9/r2.anchor: في إمام مبين ﴾ وهو اللوح المحفوظ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r1.claim: إنا نحن means that God will resurrect people after their death.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan interprets bringing them to life as bringing them from idolatry into faith.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r2.anchor: وعن الحسن : إحياؤهم : أن يخرجهم من الشرك إلى الإيمان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r3.claim: God records their prior good and bad deeds and continuing effects, such as useful knowledge, books, endowments, buildings, or harmful taxes, coinage, and practices.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r3.anchor: وما هلكوا عنه من أثر حسن ، كعلم علموه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r4.claim: He links what people leave behind to the verse saying that a person will be told what he sent ahead and left behind.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r4.anchor: ونحوه قوله تعالى : { ينبأ الإنسان يومئذ بما قدم وأخر }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes آثارهم as the footsteps of people walking to mosques.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : هي آثار المشائين إلى المساجد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r6.speaker: جابر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r6.claim: Jabir reports that Banu Salama planned to move nearer the mosque; the Prophet told them to stay, since their footsteps were recorded, and they accepted the distance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r6.anchor: وعن جابر : أردنا النقلة إلى المسجد والبقاع حوله خالية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r7.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r7.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz says that if God overlooked anything, He would overlook footsteps erased by the winds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r7.anchor: وعن عمر بن عبد العزيز : لو كان الله مغفلا شيئا لأغفل هذه الآثار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r8.claim: الإمام refers to the Preserved Tablet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r8.anchor: والإمام : اللوح . وقرىء : ( ويكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r9.claim: One reading has the verb passive, يُكْتَبُ, and reads كل شيء in the nominative.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p9#2/r9.anchor: وقرىء : ( ويكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم ) على البناء للمفعول
